What makes you think you have the right to comment on another woman’s body?”

This admonition, and hundreds of others like it, has been cropping up a lot recently. Once upon a time, it would have been in response to trolls taking aim at a woman deemed too fat. Now, it’s being deployed against users expressing concern for women deemed too thin, a social media storm sparked after Ariana Grande was “called out” over her weight after the release of the music video for “Petal”, at the end of last month.

It is, in theory, a good sentiment: your body is nobody else’s business. We have lived through countless iterations of women in the public eye being torn to shreds in the media, their appearances dissected and scorned, their every imperfection circled in red and splashed across magazines and internet pages in high definition.

In an ideal world, body neutrality would be the norm, and we would be able to simply live our lives without comment or censure, no matter what the vessel we happen to be moving through the world in looks like. The problem is, we don’t live in an ideal world – far from it.

It has been impossible not to notice the way that the arrival of GLP-1 drugs – initially developed to treat Type 2 diabetes but now widely available off-label for weight loss – has coincided with a shockingly skinny aesthetic taking over the world of female celebrity. Whether or not these particular women have been on weight loss jabs themselves is irrelevant; the introduction of Ozempic, Mounjaro and the rest has ushered in a new era in which noticeably shrinking down is fashionable, and there is seemingly no such thing as too thin.

open image in gallery Some celebrities, like singer Lizzo, have been vocal advocates for body neutrality ( Getty )

Multiple times over the past month I’ve audibly gasped at the sight of a beloved singer or actor: the jut of her collarbone; the sharp edges of her shoulders; the hard bumps of her ribcage; the nobs of every vertebra along her spine. Skeletons designed to be hidden by flesh are suddenly made visible, papered over by nothing more than fragile skin.

Some have called it a throwback to the size zero culture of the Noughties, when the grotesquely named “heroin chic” trend was held up as the warped ideal of feminine beauty. I’d argue this latest resurgence is even worse – in part, because one of the tenets of the too-short-lived body positivity movement that gained momentum in the 2010s has been hijacked and co-opted to condone and even support toxic thinness, tying us all up in knots.

That movement taught us that “commenting on people’s bodies is wrong”, whatever they look like – so the only option is to stay silent and pretend that the latest craze is normal. This stance, it seems to me, is fast becoming far more dangerous than calling out that what we’re witnessing is anything but.

This isn’t about body shaming individuals or diagnosing them with eating disorders or other illnesses, be it physical or mental, when we have neither any credentials to speak of nor access to a stranger’s medical records. No one wants to make another woman’s life harder by subjecting her to more scrutiny and pressure – particularly when she may already be unwell.

Failing to even mention the tiny elephant in the room has the potential to cause real and lasting harm

And none of these women exists in a vacuum. They are all victims of the same twisted culture that tells twentysomethings they need “preventative” Botox and fortysomethings they need facelifts; that our bodies are a series of problems to be “fixed” by spending the requisite amount of money on drugs, diets, tweakments and treatments to stay forever smaller and smoother.

It’s why I’m loath to specifically call out many of the celebrities in question in this article – though I’ll wager a few immediately sprang to mind for you regardless.

Failing to mention the tiny elephants in the room, however, can cause real and lasting harm. Worse still are the headlines that acknowledge yet normalise what we’re seeing, referring to certain women as looking “toned”. When we can see the very sinews holding together a person’s arm, that is not “toned”; that is surely a body in or approaching starvation mode.

When those pictures pop up on my news feed and people say nothing or applaud the “body transformations” on display, I can’t help but view all this through the eyes of my nieces, aged seven and 10. I imagine them exposed to this imagery while being told by the world, be it explicitly or implicitly, that looking this way is natural or healthy or glamorous #goals. I quail at them being bombarded with stick-thin figures, only achieved by a woman who eats so little that her body starts eating itself, and informed that this is what beauty looks like in 2026.

In the end, I simply cannot sit back and allow them to absorb a dialogue that holds up malnutrition and calls it normal – or, worse still, something enviable to strive for.

open image in gallery GLP-1s are helping drive the skinny aesthetic ( PA )

Of course, everyone’s body is different and some people are born into skinnier frames. What we’ve seen playing out in the world of A-listers recently is something else entirely. These are women who once looked healthy and nourished who swiftly swap that for emaciated. It’s as if they’re fading away before our very eyes.

It’s important, too, that we consider the context to all of this. The connection between women’s size and politics was popularised nearly 50 years ago in psychotherapist Susie Orbach’s seminal 1978 book, Fat is a Feminist Issue. Thinness and the patriarchy go hand in hand, she argued: making us feel insecure about our bodies is a simple way to distract and control us; making us feel like we should physically take up less space in the world is a neat metaphor for keeping us quiet and submissive. (If you’re starving all the time, are you really going to have the energy to challenge systemic inequality? Or be strong enough to run away from a predator, for that matter?)

Sadly, things have only further deteriorated since the Seventies’ revolutionary second-wave feminism when we consider the beauty “work” women are expected to perform on a daily basis to remain palatable. Social media and the subsequent rise of the beauty and wellness influencer have introduced yet more unattainable standards to fall short of – 12-step skin regimens, hour-long contouring make-up routines and 5am exercise classes – alongside the proliferation of cosmetic procedures now viewed as standard practice necessitated by the unpaid, full-time job of staying “hot” until we die. The worse we feel about ourselves, the more money we’ll spend trying to rectify it – and is only set to worsen as AI content floods our feeds. For how can we ever live up to perfect bodies that have never, and will never, consume a single calorie?

I feel like all the bodies I’m seeing online are tiny, and I’m not talking about naturally slim – I’m talking emaciated Phoebe, aka @afitnesshun

It doesn’t feel like a coincidence that a return to skinny being in vogue has gone hand-in-hand with the upsurge in both the “tradwife” movement and the manosphere to the rolling back of reproductive rights in the US and a regressive president who finds nothing wrong with commenting openly on women’s looks and whether they are smiling enough or not. The message is clear for women: shut up and stay small.

The one thing that’s given me hope in the past few weeks is seeing women – normal-sized, healthy, happy women – intentionally making and sharing videos of their bodies – normal-sized, healthy, happy bodies – on social media. These posts show their tummies and paunches, their lumps, bumps and rolls, minus any sucking in or filters to help remind us what a regular person – the kind we see every day outside on the street but rarely online – actually looks like.

“The internet is making me feel like I’m going insane,” shared Phoebe, whose Instagram handle is @afitnesshun, in a post earlier this month that’s since gone viral. “Just in case you needed to see it today, here is a very, very, very normal body.”

Dressed in a crop top and shorts, she gives a 360-degree view, continuing: “I feel like all the bodies I’m seeing online are tiny, and I’m not talking about naturally slim – I’m talking emaciated.” Training for a third marathon, Phoebe says she’s the fittest she’s ever been, and yet “I still have a stomach that sticks out, my body moves and jiggles and that is so normal – this is not something to be scared of.”

Her video garnered tens of thousands of likes and comments, most of which were positive. However, it wasn’t long before negative responses started filtering through, such as “Why are we celebrating being overweight?”; “Yes you may be healthy but that doesn’t mean your body looks good”; and “That’s not normal, that’s naturally gross.”

It perfectly demonstrated how warped our perception of women’s bodies has become, argued Phoebe in a follow-up video. “People are not viewing normal bodies as healthy bodies,” she said.

It’s not the fault of the individual women who have adopted the ultra-skinny aesthetic, and it’s not up to us to name, shame and blame them. But we equally can’t stay silent when the prevalence of eating disorders in 11- to 16-year-olds increased five-fold from 0.5 per cent in 2017 to 2.6 per cent in 2023, according to NHS England data. We need to be louder and take up more space than ever.

For now, the antidote might just be encouraging young people (and ourselves) to put down the phone and take a look around at the people they know – their friends, family and communities – and remind ourselves that, as Phoebe says: “The goal is not to be tiny. The goal is always to be the happiest, the healthiest, the fittest – and have the most fun.”

For anyone struggling with the issues raised in this article, eating disorder charity Beat’s helpline is available 365 days a year on 0808 801 0677. NCFED offers information, resources and counselling for those suffering from eating disorders, as well as their support networks. Visit eating-disorders.org.uk or call 0845 838 2040.

News.content:

Chinese president Xi Jinping is likely to attend next month's Brics summit in New Delhi with a large delegation, three sources said, in what would be his first visit in seven years and a fresh sign of a thaw between the rivals.

India is hosting the 12 to 13 September summit, where Mr Xi's presence would be watched less for the Brics (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa) agenda than for what it signals about Beijing and New Delhi's efforts ⁠to stabilise relations after deadly border clashes in 2020.

The world's two most populous nations, both nuclear powers, share a roughly 3,800km (2,400mile), largely un-demarcated and disputed border in the Himalayas.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

"Chinese officials are busy finalising hotels and security protocols," one of the Indian sources with direct knowledge told Reuters.

Last year, Indian prime minister Narendra Modi visited China for the first time in seven years, but the relationship has only improved gradually. More recently, a fresh border-related dispute triggered sharp diplomatic exchanges between the two sides.

Two other Indian ‌sources said Mr Xi was likely to be accompanied by a delegation of about 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 officials the last time in 2019.

Officials from both countries are expected to use the summit to explore ways to expand engagement while managing long-standing differences over the border and regional security issues, the sources added. Mr Xi's final travel plans and agenda for any potential bilateral between India and China are yet to be finalised, the sources said.

The Chinese foreign ministry said, "China attaches great importance to and ⁠actively participates in Brics cooperation, and supports India, the current chair, in successfully hosting this year's BRICS summit."

"We currently have no information available to provide" about Mr Xi's visit, it said.

Mr Xi missed the last Brics summit in 2025 in Brazil.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

India's foreign ministry did not comment.

Decades of relative peace along the border were shattered by 2020 clashes where 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed. The incident led to a four-year military standoff before reaching a disengagement pact in October 2024.

But on August 12, India said peace along the border was critical to ties after reports that Indian and Chinese army patrols came face-to-face in late July near a remote border.

India's ⁠national security advisor, Ajit Doval, on Monday started his visit to Beijing to meet Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi to hold talks ‌on the boundary issue.

While India and China remain competitors, US president Donald Trump's trade policies have created one area of convergence, making Mr Xi's attendance a signal that neither side wants external pressure to undermine Brics.

News.title: Help us test binoculars with the RSPB and birding experts
News.content:
At Telegraph Recommended, we test hundreds of products each year, and we rely on our community members to help verify our experts’ findings.

We currently have an upcoming opportunity for Telegraph readers to help test the latest binoculars for birdwatching with the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB).

Selected readers will be invited to RSPB’s The Lodge nature reserve in Sandy, Bedfordshire, where Jamie Wyver, editor of the RSPB magazine, and Tim Jones, otherwise known as ‘Begin Birding’ on Instagram, will host two binocular testing mornings.

Taking place on September 23 and 24, Jamie and Tim will lead each group on a morning ramble across the heathland, offering the chance to spot local bird species, including Nightjars, Hobbies and Spotted Flycatchers.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”



Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.



Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.



There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.



It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

Sports.title: Three points from Chelsea’s win over Fulham as Enzo Fernandez CAN have future at club and major transfer message sent
Sports.content:
CHELSEA kicked off their Premier League campaign and the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-2 win at neighbours Fulham.

The exciting trio of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers were all on display – and all firing.



But Robert Sanchez’s blunders cost the Blues two goals at the other end.

SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield gives his three talking points from Craven Cottage…



CURSE CANCELLED

Chelsea have grown from last season, it seems.

Last season they would have thrown this away and bottled it with a red card in the second half.

They’ve spent money, they’ve got new players, a new manager, a new system, and it seems like things are different this season.

One of those things that has changed is this supposed No9 curse at Stamford Bridge, and Joao Pedro is the man who is putting an end to that.

His opening goal inside 31 seconds was absolutely sublime, and his assist for Cole Palmer was just as good, just as full of quality.

He showed the type of player he is, the type of complete striker he has become since moving to Chelsea.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And there is clearly no more curse, because he is the one who breaks the spell.

REPLACE ROB & TRUST JOSH

One thing they do need to sort out is Robert Sanchez in goal.

This was a really disappointing display.



Emiliano Martinez is out there – Aston Villa have signed Zion Suzuki. Pay the money!

If you want to be a serious team this season and compete for the title, Chelsea need to get rid of Sanchez and need to sign a serious top-class goalkeeper.

One player who looked like he could compete in this division is Josh Acheampong.

He hasn’t been given too many minutes since he broke through from the Chelsea Cobham academy system – or CNG as it’s now called.

He was brilliant at Fulham.



Among the three defenders, in terms of actually defending, Acheampong was the best of the three.

He’s still young, he can grow into this team, he can develop in this team.

He’s a brilliant young defender who wasn’t given the opportunity to play all that much last season, but I think he should be from now on.



NOT THE ENZ AFTER ALL?

And the last talking point: is there an Enzo Fernandez problem?

He was loudly booed by everyone inside Craven Cottage who wasn’t supporting Chelsea, but cheered by his own fans.

He was okay when he came on, he wasn’t exceptional.

But the reception showed that he can still be accepted at Stamford Bridge.

If he decides he wants to play for Chelsea, that future is still there for him.



What was interesting is that he was benched for Romeo Lavia in the absence of Moises Caicedo.

So it looks like, at this point, Caicedo, Lavia and Reece James are all ahead of him in the midfield pecking order.

That is somewhat concerning.



It’d be interesting to know Alonso’s reasoning – if it’s a personnel thing or if it’s a personal thing between Alonso and Fernandez.

It remains to be seen whether he’ll stay – if he wants to stay – or if that move to Manchester City will happen before the window concludes.

But Chelsea have grown.

A good game, a good win, three goals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The most exciting front three in the Premier League, for my money, was on display, and it looks that way going into this season.



But they’ve got issues to fix if they want to be competing at the very top and show just how much they’ve grown.

Sports.title: ‘Did you not watch the game?’ – Cole Palmer in cheeky response to Sky Sports reporter after Chelsea’s win over Fulham
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER gave a cheeky response when he was asked how prepared he is for the season after spearheading Chelsea to all three points against Fulham.

The Blues got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to the perfect start as they notched a 3-2 victory at Craven Cottage.



And Palmer, 24, was the star of the show as he bagged what proved to be the winner in the West London derby.

The Chelsea livewire then showed his comedic side when he showed up for post-match media duties alongside fellow goalscorer Morgan Rogers after the final whistle.



Sky Sports reporter Emma Saunders asked: “How ready are you this season?”

Palmer, who was a shock absentee from England’s 26-man squad for the World Cup, replied: “Did you not watch the game?



“I’m only joking. I’m ready. It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot.

“But through the summer and since I’ve been back [for pre-season], I’ve worked extra hard.

“Obviously, I worked on the injuries that I had to prevent them happening again. When I work hard day in, day out, I know the talent I’ve got.

“Normally I’m not really an emotional person. I’m not really too bothered about many things in life. But over the summer I was recharged. I’m ready and I’m hungry.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Palmer grabbed an assist as Joao Pedro wrote his name into the history books in the narrow win over Fulham.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Joao Pedro makes mockery of No9 curse as Sanchez shows new keeper needed after win over Fulham
Sports.content:
Chelsea might be a little cold, after all.

Joao Pedro got Chelsea‘s season off to the perfect start after just 31 seconds with a delightful chip over Bernd Leno, having been set up by Cole Palmer in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage.



But with the lead in their hands, Chelsea showed the same signals of distress that we saw under Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane – a lack of discipline and too many silly mistakes.

Josh King bought the scores level with a powerful effort after 23 minutes, but Robert Sanchez should have done better to stop it.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

With Chelsea in need of a goal before half-time to calm things down, enter stage left, Morgan Rogers.

Maxence Lacroix could have got a nose bleed with how high up the pitch he found himself, but instead weaved his way into the box and delivered the ball across the box for Rogers to finish.

With Pedro and Rogers on the scoresheet, it was time for Palmer to join in the action.

Pedro controlled the ball brilliantly and held it up just as well before laying the ball off to his team-mate who slotted through Leno’s legs to give the Blues breathing room and wrap up the win despite another Fulham goal from Gonzalo Garcia.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 2

Not again, Rob. Please. Don’t give Chelsea fans another season of this.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Didn’t look assured at the back for the Blues, with some questionable passes out from the back, before a really poor bit of shot stopping for Josh King’s equaliser.

His role in Fulham’s second goal was not so disastrous, but still not good enough as he palmed the ball out to Gonzalo Garcia to score a goal which got Fulham back into the game again.

A few routine catches and saves is not good enough, Chelsea need a new goalkeeper in order to not undermine an otherwise good transfer window.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 8

Made several crucial blocks and clearances, particularly with the score at 1-1 to keep the Blues in the game.

Was probably Chelsea’s best actual defender in the back three tonight, with the other two struggling a little in this system – one of his best performances in a Blue shirt and he should be rewarded with more minutes.



MAXENCE LACROIX – 7

His first competitive game for Chelsea saw him look a little bit unsure of himself on the ball to start with, but he certainly sorted those issues out before half-time with a wonderful assist for Morgan Rogers first Premier League goal in Chelsea blue.

Really grew as the game went on.

LEVI COLWILL – 3

Levi Colwill was perhaps a little fortunate not to be sent off in the opening ten minutes after a poorly timed tackle on Oscar Bobb after mis-controlling a pass from his teammate.



He’s usually such a consistent performer, but tonight really wasn’t his night, and there was a case to be made for him being sent off on a second occasion in the first half too.

He was caught out of position for Fulham’s second goal too, and just looked out of sorts from the off in this game.

MALO GUSTO – 4

The less threatening of Chelsea’s wingbacks, he was far from convincing despite some decent moments.

It was quite a quiet day for the Frenchman, but in his role you want someone loud who is making things happen, and Blues fans will be excited to see Marco Palestra or even Pedro Neto there instead.

JORREL HATO – 6

Was better than Gusto, particularly going forwards, but had some shaky moments defensively, it’s hard to see where he fits in this Chelsea team long term, as he would ideally be the left sided player in a back three, where Levi Colwill plays.



A real mixed bag from the Dutchman.

ROMEO LAVIA – 6

The role of replacing Moises Caicedo is not an easy one to fill.

Got booked after 11 minutes for a bad tackle on Calvin Bassey who was breaking out from the back for Fulham – and walked the tightrope for the rest of the game quite well.

Almost put Chelsea 2-1 up in the first half when his close range effort following a set-piece was denied by Bernd Leno.

REECE JAMES – 6

Was far from the standout performer, but quietly quite good, the captain.



Influences the game in an attacking and defensive dynamic when he is at his best, and wasn’t quite there today, but still showed his quality and stepped up in midfield with Caicedo out and Enzo Fernandez on the bench.

COLE PALMER – 9

Cole Palmer is back.

With so much conversation about Palmer over the summer, an assist just 31 seconds into the new season will do the Chelsea number 10 a world of good.

He was full of confidence after the opening goal, and looked desperate for one of his own, although he was perhaps a little too greedy at times – a lesson he seemed to learn when he was also involved in Chelsea’s second.

Trying too hard can sometimes be the enemy of progress, but not today for ice-cold Cole, whose consistent and overwhelming effort saw him sprint past Joao Pedro and claim a goal of his own in the second half.



MORGAN ROGERS – 7

The new £117million man bagged on his first competitive Chelsea start after some brilliant work from Lacroix, and might have to pay a fee to Cole Palmer for using his trademarked celebration in the aftermath.

He was caught off guard defensively for Josh King’s equaliser, but all was forgiven when he found the back of the net 18 minutes later.

JOAO PEDRO – 9

Number nine curse who?



It took just 31 seconds for Joao Pedro to get off the mark this season, with a delightful chip over the goalkeeper after latching onto Cole Palmer’s through ball.

His assist for Chelsea’s third, as he repaid the favour to Cole Palmer, was full of just as much quality.

A great touch, a great run and a great lay-off showed why he is turning into such a complete number nine.

He thought he had a second late on, but for the offside flag.

SUBS:

ENZO FERNANDEZ (ROMEO LAVIA, 65) – 5

Kept things ticking nicely when he came on, but was far from exhilarating.



He was booed by anyone in the stadium not supporting Chelsea, but that reaction didn’t seem to bother him too much.

PEP CHAVARRIA (JORREL HATO, 65) – 6

Was solid after replacing Hato on the left for Chelsea, with the Blues seeming a little more assured, although the missed Hato’s attacking presence to a degree.

PEDRO NETO (MALO GUSTO, 76) – 5

Didn’t have much time to make a big impact, but did what was required of him in working hard defensively out wide.

GEOVANY QUENDA (MORGAN ROGERS, 83) – 6

An exciting double change saw he and Estevao introduced together, as supposedly the next generation of exciting Chelsea talents in attack, replacing Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He showed flashes of pace and a willingness to defend, and would have been involved in a late Joao Pedro goal, but for the offside flag.



ESTEVAO (COLE PALMER, 83) – N/A

Similarly to Quenda, he didn’t have much time to make an impact, but always looks good on the ball and gets fans up for it.

Sports.title: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3: Cole Palmer back to his best as he, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers win thriller at Craven Cottage
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S front three decided a brilliant game with a performance to send shivers down the spines of their rivals.

But Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez had the same effect on his own supporters as another gaffe-filled display helped Fulham play a full part in a classic derby.



There is rarely a dull moment on or off the field at Stamford Bridge.

And if this game is anything to go by, Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea are going to be a brilliant watch for neutrals this season – for good reasons and bad.



In Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and new signing Morgan Rogers, Alonso has potentially the best attacking unit in the Premier League.

All three scored, Pedro after 31 seconds to give the new manager a dream start.



But Sanchez was at fault for Josh King’s equaliser and for the Gonzalo Garcia goal which made it 3-2 after Rogers and Palmer had found the net either side of half-time.

Just like last season under two permanent managers and one interim boss, Chelsea looked incapable of controlling a game.

But unlike so many matches in the chaotic 2025-26 campaign, the Blues were able to hold on for victory.

Chelsea arrived with bad memories of their last visit to Craven Cottage.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Days after the departure of boss Enzo Maresca in January, the Blues had Marc Cucurella sent off in a 2-1 defeat.

As the rain lashed down, the Blues fans aimed X-rated chants at club supremo Behdad Eghbali, who was sitting next to new head coach Liam Rosenior.

Those were dark omens for a sunny summer evening.

When it emerged Moises Caicedo was out injured, the stage was set for a tough evening.

Yet after barely half a minute, Chelsea’s latest new era had the best possible start.



Maxence Lacroix’s clearing header reached Palmer, who helped the ball first time on to Pedro.

The Brazilian’s brilliant chipped finish over Bernd Leno was that of a man brimming with confidence.

The home crowd were understandably dumbstruck, the away fans jubilant.



Yet if they expected their team’s nerves to be settled, they were to be disappointed.

The normally reliable Levi Colwill miscontrolled a routine pass, Oscar Bobb nipped in, and the Blues defender was booked for stopping him running clear.

Romeo Lavia soon followed Colwill into the book for a hefty foul on Calvin Bassey.



Sanchez also gave notice of what was to come.

First the Chelsea ‘keeper let a backpass go out for a corner, then he made an unconvincing save from a King shot.

Although Palmer, Rogers and Pedro remained menacing and were one good pass away from extending Chelsea’s lead, the arrival of the equaliser was no surprise.

Rogers’ failure to go with his runner allowed King to execute a simple one-two with Timothy Castagne.

Sanchez’s positioning looked wrong and his limp-wristed attempt to stop the ball beating him at his near post was even worse.



Chelsea were rattled.

Josh Acheampong, playing instead of the suspended Wesley Fofana, made two crucial challenges to stop the home team going in front.

The visitors regained their composure and Pedro volleyed wide from a Palmer cross.

Leno saved comfortably from Reece James, then less so from Lavia, before Rogers restored the lead.



Palmer found Lacroix with a cute pass and the centre-back dropped his shoulder, beat Jorge Cuenca and pulled the ball back perfectly past Leno into the centre of the area.

Rogers redeemed himself for his part in the equaliser by sidefooting home.

Palmer upped the ante after the break.

After a mesmerising run which deserved a better finish, he made no mistake with his next chance.



Pedro ran from his own half and waited for Palmer to join him.

The Chelsea No10, from a narrow angle, fired through Leno’s legs.



Moments later it was almost 4-1, but Antonee Robinson stopped Rogers capitalising on Jorrel Hato’s surging run and cross.

Instead it was soon 2-3.

Colwill misjudged a cross and Sanchez could only parry Castagne’s shot straight on to the head of Garcia, who did not know much about his debut goal but cared even less.

Every drama needs a villain.

Enter Enzo Fernandez.



He and fellow Argentinian Valentin Barco had been roundly booed earlier in the evening, but Fernandez’s introduction in place of Lavia with 25 minutes to go took the abuse to new X-rated levels.



But some away fans sang their player’s name, despite knowing he would love to be at Manchester City before the end of the window.

After a lull, Fulham went again, with King dragging a shot wide of Sanchez’s right-hand post.

Bassey was booked for diving in the penalty area, then Robinson raced clear of James, only to send his shot over Sanchez but wide.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Chelsea ‘keeper kept out an effort by substitute Ryan Sessegnon and Pedro had a late effort ruled out for offside.

But the Blues are up and running, and it promises to be a fun ride.

Sports.title: Premier League’s 11,000-capacity stadium NOT READY for weekend clash as builders work round clock on new additions

Sports.content:

Arsenal, fresh from securing Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa, could revisit their long‑standing interest in Julian Álvarez, a player Mikel Arteta has admired for some time.

Manchester City are closing in on Palmeiras winger Allan, who made his final appearance for the Brazilian club on Sunday. Meanwhile, Savinho and Omar Marmoush are edging towards moves to Tottenham Hotspur.

Across Manchester, United have agreed a deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba but remain in the hunt for a new left‑back. Michael Carrick's side have reportedly contacted Barcelona to explore a move for Alejandro Balde.

Make sure you stay up to date with all the latest transfer news and more here at The Mirror.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher lays bare Liverpool's major Florian Wirtz issue - ‘It’s not working’
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher lays bare Liverpool's major Florian Wirtz issue - ‘It’s not working’

Florian Wirtz has had a tough time of things since joining Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen and Reds icon Jamie Carragher has now questioned why he was brought to the club in the first place

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has given his take on Florian Wirtz's disappointing time at Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has claimed that Florian Wirtz does not fit into the Liverpool team after his less-than-inspiring start to life at Anfield.

‌



The German midfielder was signed for a huge fee of £116m last season. But he had an inconsistent debut campaign. Wirtz scored seven times and notched ten assists, but was criticised for his lack of involvement.

‌



The 23-year-old had a miserable start to this season, having been hauled off after just over an hour in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle. In assessing his performance, Liverpool icon Carragher has claimed that there is no place for Wirtz in the side under Andoni Iraola.

‌



“What to do with Wirtz?” Carragher said on Sky Sports. “I’ve been seen as critical of Florian Wirtz maybe last season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“This thing that it takes players a year to settle in the Premier League, I think, is a bit of a myth. I don’t think there’s too many examples. When I see people say he’s got to be number 10, that means Szoboszlai has to be in the team in central midfield. He is not a central midfield player.

‌



“I thought this would come up in six weeks; I think it’s coming up right now. I don’t see where he fits in at all in the team. I thought I’d be having that conversation in four or six weeks. I’m looking at it right now thinking, ‘What’s Iraola going to do with this?’ You can’t keep going with it. It’s not working. It didn’t work last season. I just think it’s getting into the stage that he doesn’t fit in.

“I always thought you could put him in a pocket on the left like he does for Germany but Iraola likes wingers, likes energy.

"I don't think we're seeing a massive underperformance. I think what we've seen for a year is probably what he is, which is a neat and tidy footballer. Not a player who should be worth £110m, someone who probably should be £50m-60m, something like that. Neat and tidy, lovely touch. I'm not sure what people are expecting."

‌



View 2 Images Florian Wirtz has had a difficult time at Liverpool so far (Image: Getty Images)

Carragher’s colleague Gary Neville also offered his take on the Liverpool playmaker. And he suggested that it was down to the German midfielder to show his true self - not Iraola.

Speaking on the Gary Neville Podcast, he said: "He needs to sort himself out. Enough's enough now, we've talked about him enough. He's young and he's come to a different country -- and I'm all for willing him on.

‌



"I can see a real player there, but I can't keep watching this stuff and he's been subbed after an hour and they need a goal, but they're 2-1 down, so that's not right.

"I don't see the tenacity in Wirtz, in particular. I see a nice player moving around the pitch not really ever looking like he is busting a gut to do anything. I want to put a rocket up him because there is ability there, there is talent there, the understanding of his position.

"I just feel like Wirtz had to really think about being involved in the build up less, think about being the second striker rather than the third midfield player and the output of what he has to do."

Sports.title: New-look Chelsea deliver for Xabi Alonso - but familiar issue rears its head in Fulham win
Sports.content:
New-look Chelsea deliver for Xabi Alonso - but familiar issue rears its head in Fulham win

FULHAM 2-3 CHELSEA: Xabi Alonso's side put on a real attacking show in the Spaniard's first game in charge in the Premier League with Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro all on target

View 3 Images Chelsea put Fulham to the sword at Craven Cottage (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

The more things change, the more they stay the same.

‌



Chelsea provided a tantalising glimpse of their potential as Xabi Alonso’s new-look Blues produced a sensational attacking performance. Record buy Morgan Rogers scored on his debut and Chelsea looked the real deal going forward with fellow attackers Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer also on target.

‌



But two howlers from Chelsea's error-prone keeper Robert Sanchez let Fulham back into the contest and it is incredible how a club can spend so much money and yet still not address their most obvious weakness.

‌



Chelsea may yet be the closest challengers to Arsenal’s crown but until they sort themselves out at the back their forwards will have to carry on working overtime.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sense of excitement around Xabi Alonso’s new-look Chelsea has completely overshadowed the nerves surrounding Alvaro Arbeloa’s reign at Fulham.

‌



Chelsea have broken the bank again with another raft of big-money deals - including British record signing Morgan Rogers for £117m - and brought in a big-name manager.

By comparison, Fulham equalled their record signing with a £34m move for Gonzalo Garcia who followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid. But Arbeloa feels like a gamble from six months in charge at Real Madrid to succeeding Marco Silva’s five-year reign at Craven Cottage.

The gap between the two clubs is huge - and the last thing Chelsea needed was a head start. But that is exactly what they got. The Blues were ahead after just 31 seconds. Fulham defender Jorge Cuenca’s clearance was headed back by Maxence Lacroix and Cole Palmer provided the clever flick-on.

‌



Joao Pedro went clean through, kept his composure brilliantly and then lifted the ball over Fulham keeper Bernd Leno and into the empty net. Even the Chelsea fans in the away end could hardly believe it.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers enjoyed a dream debut for Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Fulham fans were nervous and you could sense the tension in the air - together with a smattering of boos - when Chelsea threatened to expose the home side’s defensive frailties. Arbeloa’s men very much look like a work in progress at the back.

‌



Chelsea had a let-off when Levi Colwill only got a booking for cynically scything down Oscar Bobb but it did serve to whip up the home fans. This wonderful old stadium creates such a great atmosphere.

It was Fulham teenager Josh King who fed off the energy. King’s low shot beat Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez at his near post to bring Fulham level after 23 minutes.

It was a horrible moment for the Chelsea keeper. It was an absolute howler. It is incredible that, despite spending so much money, Chelsea have stuck with an error-prone keeper who has let them down on so many occasions.

‌



Chelsea got themselves back in front before the break when two big money buys combined. Chelsea’s £52m defender Lacroix pushed forward, his low cross found Rogers and the record buy drilled home. What an introduction.

View 3 Images Cole Palmer also scored in Chelsea's win (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea gave themselves a two-goal cushion after the break. Sanchez’s long clearance was flicked on by Rogers, Joao Pedro played in Palmer and the Chelsea forward brilliantly nutmegged Leno at his near post.

‌



It looked as if Chelsea would take charge. But Sanchez struck again. Sanchez could not hold Timothy Castagne’s shot, the ball sprung up and there was Garcia to head home on his debut.

It was game-on. And the noise got even louder when Enzo Fernandez came on to huge boos as the Fulham fans gave the Argentina midfielder pelters as he might just be the most unpopular player in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Furious Leandro Trossard hits out at officials after ex-Arsenal star SLAPPED in game
Sports.content:
Furious Leandro Trossard hits out at officials after ex-Arsenal star SLAPPED in game

Leandro Trossard is getting to grips with life in Turkey after leaving Arsenal last month but was embroiled in controversy during Besiktas' loss to Alanyaspor on Sunday

View Image Leandro Trossard was struck by an opponent during Besiktas' 1-0 loss to Alanyaspor

Leandro Trossard and Besiktas have condemned the 'disgraceful' refereeing in their match with Alanyaspor after an opposition player evaded punishment despite appearing to slap the former Arsenal attacker in the face.

‌



Trossard completed a transfer to the Turkish Super Lig last month and Sunday's 1-0 defeat to Alanyaspor was just his second league game for Besiktas. Unfortunately, the 32-year-old was involved in the major talking point of the match for all the wrong reasons after getting caught up in an off the ball incident with Fidan Aliti.

‌



Video replays showed the Swiss defender clearly struck Trossard in the face after a coming together - but he was spared punishment by referee Adnan Deniz Kayatepe and VAR, much to the shock of the Belgium international.

‌



Trossard fumed after the game: "The decision should clearly have been changed; I think the opponent slapped me. Clear red card. The decision needed to be changed."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Besiktas went one further in a scathing statement where they singled out Kayatepe and Bulent Birincioglu, the game's designated VAR official.

‌



In a post shared on X, the club wrote: "The management displayed by the referees in our match against Corendon Alanyaspor has taken its place in history as a document of shame for Turkish refereeing.

"Adnan Deniz Kayatepe, the prince of the Central Referee Committee president whose scandalous decisions in last year's Ziraat Turkish Cup semi-final still linger fresh in memories, has added yet another disgraceful performance to his record, as if to say, 'Where did we leave off?'

‌



"The opposing player slapped Trossard right in front of the world's eyes. Referee Adnan Deniz Kayatepe failed to see the incident. Bülent Birincioğlu in the VAR room, meanwhile, remained silent.

"We do not want to see malicious referees like Adnan Deniz Kayatepe and Bülent Birincioğlu in our matches ever again.

Sports.title: Arsenal close to completing record transfer deal after Mikel Arteta green light
Sports.content:
Arsenal close to completing record transfer deal after Mikel Arteta green light

Arsenal have spent heavily in the transfer market this summer but the Gunners could add to their coffers just before the deadline with a few sales potentially in the pipeline

View 2 Images Arsenal's summer transfer business might not be totally over (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are close to selling Brazilian winger Gabriel Martinelli in what would represent a record sale for the Premier League champions.

‌



Martinelli, 25, has been linked with a move to Saudi Arabia over recent days, with Al-Hilal chasing his services. Arsenal have held talks with their Middle Eastern counterparts over recent days, while the winger was left out of Mikel Arteta’s 18-man squad for their opening day victory against Coventry at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



It now appears that a move is close with football.london claiming Arsenal and Al-Hilal are nearing an agreement for Martinelli’s services. He is expected to leave the club for a substantial fee in the region of £50million.

‌



That would make the deal the most lucrative sale in Arsenal history - eclipsing the £35m they were previously paid by Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain back in 2017.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Martinelli would leave after a seven-year spell in North London, having joined the club from Brazilian side Ituano. Since then, he has made 278 appearances for the club and has scored 62 times, helping Arsenal win the Premier League last season.

‌



The forward had entered the final 12 months of his Arsenal deal, albeit there was an option to extend that by a further campaign. Galatasaray had initially expressed an interest in him, albeit decided to end their pursuit, which opened the door to Al-Hilal.

Martinelli would become the latest high-profile player to leave the club this summer. Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas earlier this year, while Jakub Kiwior and Christian Norgaard have both been allowed to leave.

Arsenal in the meantime have added to their frontline, with the signing of Greek international Christos Tzolis, who has enjoyed a productive start to life with his new employers after a £34m move from Club Brugge.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli looks set for a move to Saudi Arabia (Image: Getty Images)

On Tzolis, Arteta said after the win against Coventry: “I love that a player who has only been with us a few weeks gets this kind of energy whenever he’s on the ball, and I think he’s earned it. I think the way he has performed the last few games has been phenomenal; what he transmits as a player - so direct, constantly incisive and wants to make things happen.

“He has an incredible variety of actions in the last 30 metres to decide and make the right decisions - even when the spaces are really small. I’m really impressed with him.”

Article continues below

Asked if Arsenal are still keen to add to their frontline amid ongoing links with Atletico Madrid wantaway Julian Alvarez, he added: “I’m really happy with the squad that we have, and the main focus is to improve the players we already have, as we already have a lot of good things.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sets one condition for £130m Julian Alvarez transfer as Arsenal plan emerges
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sets one condition for £130m Julian Alvarez transfer as Arsenal plan emerges

Arsenal have spent heavily this summer and a move for Julian Alvarez remains a distinct possibility heading into the final week of the transfer market and Mikel Arteta has now made his stance clear

View 2 Images Alvarez was loudly booed by Atletico Madrid fans over the weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is ready to make a £130m push to sign Julian Alvarez - but will demand assurances the Argentina star wants to move to Arsenal.

‌



Atletico Madrid have become embroiled in an ugly stand-off with Alvarez which has seen the club’s own fans turn on the 26-year-old. Alvarez has been pushing for a move to Barcelona but Atletico are refusing to entertain a deal with their La Liga rivals but may now be open to doing business with Arsenal.

‌



The former Manchester City star was booed by Atletico fans during their draw with Villarreal last weekend and there may be no way back for Alvarez.

‌



The World Cup star has previously insisted he only wants Barcelona and clearly Arsenal boss Arteta would need to be convinced the striker would be fully invested in a move to the Emirates.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It would also need Arsenal to be able to balance the books with Brazil winger Gabriel Martinelli closing in on a £50m move to Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal.That would represent a record sale for the Gunners with Martinelli’s initial reluctance to go to Saudi having softened because it is clear that he is no longer central to Arteta’s plans.

‌



Arsenal also want to sell Fabio Vieira with Hamburg pushing to get a deal done while Napoli have been interested in Gabriel Jesus but the biggest stumbling block has been the Brazilian’s wages.

Jesus has also wanted to stay in England but knows his chances at Arsenal will be limited.

View 2 Images Alvarez is keen to push through a move to Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

‌



It remains to be seen whether Arsenal would even entertain a deal involving Viktor Gyokeres with Atletico Madrid but the chances of signing Juventus star Kenan Yildiz appear remote as the winger needs knee surgery.

Arsenal have already spent big in this window with Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa so it may be a very real possibility they do not do more business even if they sell Martinelli.

They do have Eberechi Eze who can fill on the left flank and may bide their time but if there is a chance of Alvarez and he is willing to move then Arsenal are open.

Sports.title: Man City 'pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez within days' as Chelsea's latest demands emerge
Sports.content:
Man City 'pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez within days' as Chelsea's latest demands emerge

Enzo Fernandez's future at Chelsea has been the subject of speculation throughout the campaign with Man City interested in the midfielder

View 2 Images Man City are reportedly pushing to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Manchester City are reportedly looking to complete the signing of Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez this week. According to Italian outlet Gianluca Di Marzio, Enzo Maresca's side are working on completing the formalities to bring the Argentinian to the Etihad Stadium.

‌



The report claims that Chelsea are asking for €140million (£120m) for the former Benfica man, with Fernandez pushing to reunite with the former Stamford Bridge chief. City are said to be in talks with Newcastle United over a move for Nico Gonzalez which would see the midfielder make the switch to the North East.

‌



Earlier this month, Chelsea set a deadline for Fernandez's departure, informing their Premier League rivals - and any possible suitors - that they had until 5pm on Friday, August 14 to seal a deal with the 25-year-old. No deal was struck and at the time, Maresca refused to be drawn on the speculation.

‌



He said: "In this moment I have to give you the same answer since day one, which will be always the same. He is a player from another club and I don't think it's correct to talk about other players.

"I'm not going to say anything about players who are not with us. Not today, to be honest. I don't think we're going to do something today."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



City came from behind to beat Bournemouth 2-1 in their Premier League opener while Chelsea make the short journey across West London to take on Fulham in their curtain-raiser. on Monday night. New head coach Xabi Alonso will be in the dugout for his first top-flight match in England when he comes up against former Liverpool teammate Alvaro Arbeloa.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

All eyes will be on the starting 11 with the Spaniard tasked with taking Chelsea back towards the upper reaches of the Premier League after a topsy-turvy few years at Stamford Bridge. Whether Fernandez is in the starting line-up or not remains to be seen with speculation mounting over his future

‌



Chelsea were said to have agreed with his agent, Javier Pastore, that he could leave the Blues for £120million if the asking price was met by the August 14 deadline.

Alonso reaffirmed the stance that the 25-year-old remains a Chelsea player. He said:" Enzo is a Chelsea player. He's a top, top player.

"He's training really well. We are happy with him and he's getting ready for Monday."

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star Samuel Eto'o bizarrely pledges support to FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea star Samuel Eto'o bizarrely pledges support to FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA President Gianni Infantino remains under huge pressure following his cancelled plan to sell a share of the World Cup to external investors but former Chelsea and Barcelona star Samuel Eto’o remains a fan

View 2 Images Samuel Eto'o has underlined his support for Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Chelsea and Everton star Samuel Eto’o has bafflingly claimed that Gianni Infantino has ‘not done anything wrong’ in the wake of the growing scrutiny on the FIFA President.

‌



Infantino, 56, remains under huge pressure following his now failed plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to external investors. He performed a rapid u-turn on the plan, albeit UEFA have already confirmed a loss of confidence in his ability to lead FIFA. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has criticised Infantino, claiming he is the wrong man to make decisions on the future of the game.

‌



A number of legendary players have now gone a step further by releasing a bombshell statement claiming that football has lost its core values under Infantino’s leadership.

‌



But one former star does not appear to be sharing that sentiment, having made clear his support of the current president.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking to CNN Sports, former Chelsea and Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o, said: “I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong. I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out, when Gianni Infantino is standing. All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.”

‌



“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” Eto’o added. “He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognize what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

While Infantino’s plan garnered wide-spread criticism, Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation, has actually claimed that it would have benefited his nation.

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino remains under serious pressure (Image: Getty Images)

“The bigger nations took up the media space. They gave their point of view, and President Gianni Infantino wanted to keep the family of football together, and he decided to withdraw the project,” he said.

“I remain convinced that for us as Africans, this project was something that could have been incredible. It would have reset the balance of power in football to ensure that our talent doesn’t disappear and end up playing for other nations.

‌



“At the end of the day, those who have talked about the project and who’ve given their opinion haven’t properly read what it’s all about, and in some cases, they looked at it from their dominant position.

He added: “I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After President Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion.

“I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Chelsea's electric front three edge out Fulham in pulsating MNF opener
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.

The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.

If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"

It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.

Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.

The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.

The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.

On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.

Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:

"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.

"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."

Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.

"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."

The key moments from Craven Cottage

1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.

23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.

41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.

49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.

54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.

65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.

78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.

82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.

What's next?

Rate the players...

Title winners

Jamie Carragher - Arsenal

A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance - but it was all around Rodri. If Rodri stayed I'd maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can't see it.

Gary Neville - Chelsea, Man City, Man Utd

Chelsea second? Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football. If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City.

I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea. I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth.

Fifth and sixth?

Jamie Carragher - Man Utd, Spurs

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi and Archie Gray believed they were outfought by Brentford but Jamie Redknapp believes that the squad selection was wrong.

Gary Neville - Liverpool, Brighton

Sometimes you look at Spurs going, 'oh, they've spent a lot of money' and thinking 'quite exciting for Spurs fans, they're finally splashing the cash'. But then I look at the team and I think, 'where's it all gone?'

Savinho and Omar Marmoush will make them a lot better, but I just don't know whether they'll pull it together and that's the question.

I know Brighton are a good unit, they're reliable, they're consistent and I think Brentford and Brighton, those two teams this season may just get in there because they're consistent and they know what they're doing and they're well-drilled.

A well-organised, well-drilled team will beat a team of talented players who are still trying to find their way.

European contender?

Jamie Carragher - Brentford

A lot of people say, when you're managing a club like Brentford, which is so well-run behind the scenes and the hierarchy, it makes it easier for the manager. Of course it does - but watching them this weekend, watching them last season...

Brentford haven't got European football, so I think that will be a big plus for them. I really love watching Brentford play, and for me, that was the best performance of the week [their win over Spurs].

Gary Neville - Spurs

Relegated

Jamie Carragher - Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland

Why Sunderland? The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday. I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal.

I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation.
