World.title: Uba Sani approves ₦300m for KASU-ASUU, sets up negotiation c’ttee to avert strike
World.content:
The Kaduna State Government has constituted a nine-member negotiation committee to engage with the Kaduna State University (KASU) chapter of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and other staff unions over their outstanding demands.

The government also approved a one-off payment of ₦300 million as Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) for academic staff of the university.

The decisions were contained in a statement issued by the Secretary to the Kaduna State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Mu’azu Meyere, on Monday.

According to the statement, the interventions are part of the administration’s efforts to resolve long-standing staff welfare and funding issues at KASU while preventing disputes that could disrupt academic activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Meyere said the ₦300 million EAA payment was part of the government’s sustained efforts to address a backlog of more than ₦800 million in accumulated entitlements and allowances dating back to 2016.

He said the intervention demonstrated Governor Uba Sani’s commitment to staff welfare, industrial harmony and the stability of the university through constructive dialogue and sustainable solutions.

Background

The latest development comes amid demands by university-based unions for improved welfare, payment of outstanding allowances and implementation of agreements affecting academic and non-academic staff.

The government said its interventions over the past three and a half years had included the settlement of outstanding withheld salaries, payment of more than ₦300 million for accreditation of academic programmes and resource-verification exercises for postgraduate programmes, and the release of funds to clear outstanding SIWES supervision allowances.

It also said the administration had established a ₦50 million monthly standing order to facilitate the systematic settlement of outstanding arrears.

The government said the measures were aimed at addressing inherited liabilities while ensuring that KASU remains financially and academically stable.

Committee to Review Union Demands

The negotiation committee will be chaired by the Commissioner for Education, Professor Abubakar Sani Sambo.

Other members are the Commissioner for Business, Innovation and Technology, Mrs Patience Fakai; Commissioner for Youth, Mrs Gloria Ibrahim; Chairman of the Local Government Service Board, Professor Ladan Sharehu; Director-General of the Kaduna State Schools Quality Assurance Authority, Professor Usman Abubakar Zaria; Vice-Chancellor of KASU, Professor Abdullahi Ibrahim Musa; and Pro-Chancellor of the university, Dr Ibrahim Umar.

The Permanent Secretary, General Services, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, is also a member, while the Permanent Secretary, Establishments Services and Training, will serve as secretary to the committee.

The committee has four weeks to complete its assignment and submit its recommendations to the state government.

It is mandated to review the demands of ASUU, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), and the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT).

Among other issues, the committee is expected to examine the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), compare KASU’s situation with prevailing practices in other state-owned universities, and assess the financial implications of implementing demands arising from the 2025 ASUU–Federal Government agreement.

Mr Meyere said the committee was expected to recommend practical, equitable and financially sustainable solutions to the outstanding issues.

Government Appeals for Dialogue

The Secretary to the State Government urged the unions to embrace dialogue, negotiation and collective bargaining rather than resorting to industrial action that could disrupt the academic calendar and adversely affect students and their families.

He said the government’s channels of engagement remained open, assuring the university community of its commitment to strengthening KASU, improving staff welfare and safeguarding uninterrupted academic activities.

The latest intervention therefore places emphasis on negotiation as the preferred route for resolving the KASU unions’ grievances, while the government seeks to balance staff demands with the state’s financial capacity.

World.title: NNPC, SNEPCo, Esso, Agip Move Towards FID, Target $21bn Inflow
World.content:
• Peak production projected at 175,000 bpd, 140 million scf/day in OML 118

• Project set to become Nigeria’s largest deep water facility

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja and Peter Uzoho in Lagos





The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and its contractor parties — Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company Limited (SNEPCo), Esso Exploration and Production Nigeria (Deepwater) Limited, and Nigerian Agip Exploration Limited (NAE) – yesterday executed the Addendum to the Oil Mining Lease (OML 118) Production Sharing Contract (PSC) and the Addendum to the Dispute Settlement Agreement (DSA).

The development marked a major milestone in the advancement of the deepwater Bonga Southwest/Aparo project (BWSAp) towards Final Investment Decision (FID).

NNPCL announced the deals in a statement signed by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Mr. Andy Odey.

The execution gives effect to the fiscal and commercial terms approved by the federal government to support the development of BSWAp and it reinforces Nigeria’s commitment to creating a competitive, stable and attractive environment for large-scale deepwater investment.

The milestone follows the approval of the Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Projects Incentives (Tax Remission) Order, 2026, by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, an important component of the government’s ongoing reforms to enhance the competitiveness of Nigeria’s deepwater sector and unlock new investment.

BSWAp is expected to attract between $15 billion and $21 billion in investment over the life of the project, with peak production projected at about 175,000 barrels of oil per day and 140 million standard cubic feet of gas per day, the national oil firm stated.

The project is expected to boost Nigeria’s oil and gas production, government revenues and foreign exchange earnings, while creating opportunities for local contractors and suppliers and supporting employment, skills development and technology transfer.

Speaking on the milestone, the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC, Bayo Ojulari, said the project will unlock a major deepwater project, demonstrating that Nigeria has a competitive fiscal framework and a clear pathway for sustainable investment in its energy sector

“The execution of the BSWAp PSC and DSA Addenda demonstrates the effectiveness of President Tinubu’s reforms in translating policy into investment. This is about unlocking a major deepwater project and demonstrating that Nigeria has a competitive fiscal framework and a clear pathway for sustainable investment in its energy sector.

“NNPC Ltd will continue to work closely with the federal government, our partners and other stakeholders to ensure that this project delivers maximum value for the federation and the Nigerian people,” he explained.

The OML 118 Contractor Parties also announced the successful completion of the project’s Pre-Front End Engineering Design (Pre-FEED) phase, which they said had helped mature the technical and commercial scope of the development and positioned it to progress into the Front End Engineering Design (FEED) phase.

However, the transition to FEED remains subject to applicable partner, assurance and governance requirements.

The partners have also identified a preferred Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) contractor following a competitive selection process. The selection, the statement said, is subject to the completion of applicable partner, regulatory, assurance and governance processes.

According to the oil company,it provides a basis for progressing the FPSO concept into FEED and undertaking further engineering and commercial work required to mature the project towards FID.

However, any eventual award of the FPSO Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Installation (EPCI) contract remains subject to all applicable approvals and requirements, it explained.

When operational, BSWAp is expected to become one of Nigeria’s most significant new deepwater production hubs and contribute materially to national oil production.

The project is also expected to generate substantial economic benefits through billions of dollars in investment, increased participation by Nigerian contractors and suppliers and direct and indirect employment opportunities across engineering, fabrication, offshore construction, logistics and operations.

The development is expected to strengthen Nigerian content by expanding contracting opportunities for indigenous companies, enhancing local fabrication, marine and engineering capabilities, facilitating technology transfer and skills development, and creating opportunities across the wider economy.

The execution of the agreements reflects collaboration among NNPC Ltd, the federal government, regulatory agencies and the OML 118 Contractor Parties as the project advances towards FID.

NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to working with all stakeholders to advance the BSWAp project safely, competitively and responsibly while maximising value for Nigeria and the Nigerian people.

World.title: Kwankwaso: APC’s Presidential Campaign Council Represents Continuous Hardship
World.content:
•You’re jittery over Yari, group fires back

•NRRM also decries Modu Sheriff’s inclusion

Adedayo Akinwale, Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja and Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano





The vice presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has described the recently constituted All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council as representing a continuation of the same system that has brought severe hardship to Nigerians.

In a statement shared on his Facebook account, Kwankwaso said the composition of the council offered Nigerians a clear picture of the choice before them in the 2027 general election. He added that the election would be a struggle between the oppressed Nigerian masses and those who had benefited from and sustained the current system.

However, an APC support group, APC Daga Titi Zuwa Titi, said Kwankwaso’s comments expressed nervousness regarding Yari’s appointment as Director-General of the APC presidential campaign council.

National Coordinator of the group, Jaafar Hassan, said in a statement that Kwankwaso’s comments were a clear indication that Yari’s emergence as the ruling party’s campaign director had unsettled the opposition.

But Nigeria Rescue and Renewal Movement (NRRM) also condemned the inclusion of former Borno State governor, Senator Ali Modu Sheriff, in the APC presidential campaign council.

NRRM National President, Comrade Aliyu Adam Usman, told journalists that the organisation was particularly worried because of Sheriff’s alleged links to the Boko Haram terrorist group.

Kwankwaso said regarding the APC presidential campaign council, “The council brings together many of the same political actors who have supported, defended or participated in the present administration.

“Their coming together raises a fundamental question: what exactly are they asking Nigerians to vote for in 2027, a new beginning, or the continuation of the same system that has brought severe hardship to our people?”

Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, lamented that families across the country were struggling with the rising cost of food and basic necessities, while young Nigerians faced unemployment and diminishing opportunities.

He stated, “Farmers and businesses are struggling to survive, while millions continue to live with insecurity. Our education, healthcare and other essential public services remain under enormous pressure.”

Kwankwaso appealed to Yari to reconsider accepting the position of Director-General of APC Presidential Campaign Council

He said, “As a former governor of Zamfara State and a prominent leader from the North-west, I believe Senator Yari has a clear understanding of the devastating consequences of insecurity, poverty, unemployment, displacement and the destruction of livelihoods in the region and the country at large.

“I, therefore, will be surprised if, in his good conscience, he will lead a campaign whose principal objective is to secure the continuation of a government under which many of the people he once governed, and other innocent Nigerians remain trapped in these challenges.”

The statement also raised concerns over the inclusion of Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr Zacch Adedeji, and Director-General of Budget Office of the Federation, Dr Tanimu Yakubu Kurfi, in the APC campaign’s fundraising and finance structures.

Kwankwaso stated that the leadership of critical public institutions demanded neutrality, integrity, and public confidence. He questioned whether the responsibilities of senior officials entrusted with managing public revenue and national finances could appropriately coexist with senior partisan campaign roles.

“The government and the APC should explain how such arrangements are consistent with institutional neutrality and public trust,” he stated.

Kwankwaso, however, expressed optimism that Nigerians would reject “continued oppression” in 2027 and demand accountable and people-centred governance.

“If Osun people can do it, so can all other parts of the country,” he said, adding, “Ultimately, no campaign council is more powerful than the Nigerian people.”

Ex-Gov Jittery over Yari’s Appointment as APC Campaign Council DG, States Group

A support group, APC Daga Titi Zuwa Titi, fired back at Kwankwaso, saying he is jittery over the appointment of Yari as Director-General of the APC presidential campaign council.

The group stated that Kwankwaso’s comments about the appointment of Yari was a clear indication that his emergence had unsettled the opposition.

National Coordinator of the group, Jaafar Hassan, in a statement, said it was revealing that out of all the appointments announced in the APC campaign structure, Kwankwaso found it necessary to personally appeal to Yari to reconsider his acceptance of the responsibility.

Hassan stated, “Politicians rarely advise their opponents to abandon positions they consider politically irrelevant.

“Senator Kwankwaso may dress his intervention in the language of brotherly concern, but Nigerians can see through it.

“You do not publicly plead with an opponent to leave the battlefield unless you are worried about what his presence on that battlefield means.”

The group maintained that Yari’s appointment had altered the political calculations of opposition leaders, particularly in the North-west, where the former Zamfara State governor had built an extensive political network and growing grassroots following.

The organisation said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu did not appoint Senator Yari to decorate a campaign list. He appointed a former two-term governor, former Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, serving Senator and experienced grassroots politician, who understands the political terrain of Northern Nigeria and has demonstrated an ability to organise, mobilise and build relationships across political and regional boundaries. That is what has made Kwankwaso uncomfortable.”

NRRM Condemns Modu Sheriff’s Inclusion in Tinubu’s Campaign Council

Nigeria Rescue and Renewal Movement (NRRM) also condemned the inclusion of former Borno State governor, Senator Ali Modu Sheriff, in APC’s Presidential Campaign Council.

Speaking with journalists, NRRM National President, Comrade Aliyu Adam Usman, said the organisation was particularly concerned about the decision because of historical allegations that had previously linked Sheriff to Boko Haram.

According to Usman, the appointment has reopened questions about political accountability and the suitability of individuals entrusted with major responsibilities in the North-east, a region that had endured years of insurgency and insecurity.

NRRM said its objection should not be interpreted as an assertion that Sheriff had been convicted of any offence or that the historical allegations had been established as facts.

Rather, the group said it was demanding greater scrutiny and accountability when political parties selected individuals to represent them in sensitive regions.

Usman stated, “Our concern is why a politician whose name has been associated with serious allegations concerning Boko Haram is being given the responsibility of coordinating the presidential campaign in the North-east, a region that has suffered tremendously from the insurgency.”

He stated that political parties should consider not only electoral calculations but also public confidence, historical controversies, and the broader interests of communities, when selecting campaign leaders.

World.title: US Imposes Sweeping New Sanctions on Iran, Targets Oil Traders, Shadow Fleet, Others
World.content:
• Vows action against countries, individuals doing business with Iran

•Iran says sanctions will fail , vows retaliation

•Oil prices fall 2.4% as market weighs China risk

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The United States yesterday imposed sweeping new sanctions on Iran, targeting its military procurement networks, petroleum and petrochemical traders, shadow fleet operators and other entities accused of helping Tehran generate revenue and sustain its military activities.

The measures, announced by the US Department of State and Treasury, came under what Washington described as “Operation Economic Outcast”, a broader campaign aimed at cutting Iran off from international financial and commercial networks.

The latest action targets nearly 60 individuals, entities and vessels, according to the US government, with the sanctions covering Iranian military activities, procurement, cyber operations and petroleum and petrochemical revenue generation.

The US said the measures were designed to restrict the revenues used by the Iranian regime to attack its neighbours, support terrorism and sustain its military capabilities.

The sanctions also target companies and intermediaries in third countries involved in the purchase, transportation and marketing of Iranian petroleum and petrochemical products.

Among those sanctioned were India-based companies accused of importing Iranian petroleum products, Turkish companies involved in petrochemical trade, a Hong Kong-based company accused of operating a tanker carrying Iranian crude, as well as an India-based customs broker.

US Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, described the campaign as an “economic onslaught” against Iran and said Washington’s objective was to sever the financial lifelines sustaining the Iranian regime.

Bessent warned that entities facilitating transactions involving Iranian oil and helping convert the country’s petroleum revenues into funds for the regime could be targeted. He also said US President Donald Trump was contacting world leaders and demanding that they cease economic interactions with Tehran.

The announcement has raised particular questions about China, Iran’s largest trading partner and a major buyer of its oil.

China has opposed unilateral sanctions and called for political and diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict, potentially setting the stage for a confrontation between Washington and Beijing over enforcement of the new measures.

But he declined to identify the countries that would be targeted or reveal when those penalties would take effect, saying he would instead provide them time to comply with the new directive.

“We are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behaviour. Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” Bessent said at a news conference.

The US also sanctioned senior Iranian military officials, including Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander Ahmad Vahidi, Khatam ol Anbia Central Headquarters commander Ali Abdollahi and IRGC Aerospace Force commander Sayyed Hosein Majid Musavi Eftekhari.

Washington accused the officials of directing or supporting Iran’s military activities, including ballistic missile and unmanned aerial vehicle programmes.

The US also designated the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Cyber-Electronic Command, accusing it of obtaining information on US military assets and facilities to support Iranian military targeting operations.

The sanctions extend beyond Iran, with Washington warning companies and individuals in other countries that facilitate Iranian oil and petrochemical transactions that they could also face restrictions.

Among the companies targeted was India-based Sadashiva Overseas Limited, which the US said imported approximately $69 million worth of Iranian-origin petroleum products between February 2024 and June 2025.

Another Indian company, PP Softtech Private Limited, was accused of importing about $25 million worth of Iranian petroleum products between January 2024 and June 2025.

Prakrutees Infra Impex India Private Limited was also sanctioned for importing Iranian petroleum products valued at about $25 million between May 2023 and February 2026.

The US further targeted Hong Kong-based Selenium Resources Limited, which Washington said exported more than $22.8 million worth of Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January 2023 and September 2024.

The measures also hit Turkey-based Huzur Plastik, which the US said imported Iranian-origin polyethylene valued at $28 million between June 2022 and May 2024.

The US said the sanctions would block the property and interests in property of designated persons that are located in the United States or controlled by US persons.

It also warned that entities owned, directly or indirectly, by blocked persons by 50 per cent or more would equally be subject to the restrictions.

The measures effectively prohibit US persons and transactions within or transiting the United States from dealing with the sanctioned individuals and entities unless authorised by the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control.

The latest sanctions formed part of a broader US attempt to intensify economic pressure on Tehran after Washington and Israel failed to achieve a decisive outcome through military action.

Iran: Sanctions Will Fail

In a reaction, Iran rejected the latest US sanctions, describing Washington’s renewed economic pressure as a sign of desperation and insisting that the measures would not force Tehran to surrender.

Iranian Foreign Minister, Abbas Araqchi, said the shift from military operations to sanctions showed that Washington was running out of options.

“The fact that they (U.S. leaders) have moved on from military operations … to bring up the same old plans shows that they are desperate,” Araqchi said.

He maintained that Iran had already endured blockades and military pressure and would withstand the latest measures.

“We have never been afraid. All of their actions – whether blockades or other military moves they have made – have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail as well,” he said.

Araqchi called instead for a settlement based on “justice and honour”.

Iranian military officials have separately threatened retaliation against countries that cooperate with the US sanctions campaign, with the response potentially involving land, sea, air or cyber operations.

The sanctions come amid the continuing crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, where disruptions to shipping have already placed pressure on global energy markets.

With Iran’s oil exports, the strategic waterway and international financial transactions now at the centre of the confrontation, the latest US measures could widen the economic consequences of the conflict beyond Washington and Tehran.

Oil Prices Fall 2.4% as Market Weighs China Risk

Meanwhile, the fresh US sanctions on Iran triggered a sharp reversal in oil prices yesterday, with Brent crude falling 2.4 per cent to $92.17 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropping 2.4 per cent to $85.01, after six consecutive sessions of gains.

Market analysts said the immediate impact of the sanctions on Iranian oil exports could be limited because Tehran’s crude shipments have already been constrained by the US blockade, while China, the principal buyer of Iranian oil, has historically resisted Washington’s sanctions.

Jorge Leon, head of geopolitical analysis at Rystad Energy, said the immediate measures appeared less dramatic than the rhetoric surrounding them, arguing that the bigger threat to global oil markets could come from Iran’s response.

“The biggest oil-market risk may not be the sanctions themselves, but Iran’s response to them,” Leon said, warning that Iran still had considerable capacity to disrupt other countries’ oil exports.

David Oxley of Capital Economics similarly said that although the sanctions were broader in scope, their immediate effect on Iranian energy flows could be limited because most of Iran’s oil exports go to China.

“In practice, though, we suspect that the new package will have only a limited direct impact on Iranian energy flows in the short term,” Oxley said.

He noted, however, that the sanctions could still have a sizeable impact on the global energy landscape depending on whether they accelerate or delay a resolution to the conflict.

The market reaction underscored the importance of China’s response to Washington’s latest measures. Beijing has opposed unilateral US sanctions and called for diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict, potentially limiting the immediate effectiveness of Washington’s attempt to isolate Tehran economically.

World.title: 2027: Otuaro Urges Ijaw Youths to Back Tinubu’s Election, Kwara Marches for Him
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja an Hammed Shittu in Ilorin





The Administrator of the Presidential Amnesty Programme, Dennis Otuaro, has urged the Ijaw Youth Council to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 elections.

Otuaro made the appeal when the newly inaugurated 10th leadership of the IYC, led by its President, Doubra Okotete, visited him at his office in Abuja.

He said supporting Tinubu for a second term was in the strategic interest of the Ijaw people and the wider Niger Delta region, while cautioning against divisions that could weaken the region’s political influence.

“My appeal to the IYC is that nothing should divide us. 2027 is already here. Let us back the President and mobilise for him to win a second term.

“We should not allow anybody to cause division among us or trade us for a new hope. It is within the Ijaw strategic national interest to support the President to secure victory,” he said.

The PAP administrator also praised the IYC and other Niger Delta stakeholders for supporting the agency’s peacebuilding initiatives and reforms.

Responding, Okotete commended the PAP under Otuaro for what he described as “unprecedented success in the education and empowerment of Niger Delta youths.”

The IYC president praised Otuaro’s management of the programme and said the council was prepared to strengthen its partnership with the PAP and explore additional areas of collaboration.

Kwara Youths March for Tinubu over Army 9 Division, Declares It’s Masterstroke

A coalition of Kwara Youth Organisations and Arewa Youth Assembly, yesterday, said, the creation of the Nigerian Army Battalion, 9 Division in Ilorin remained a strategic masterstroke that would enhance the security and economic development of the state.

They, however, lauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the creation of the Army 9 Division of Nigerian Army in Ilorin, the state capital.

The two groups, in separate interviews in Ilorin yesterday on the sidelines of the peaceful protest embarked upon by them, told newsmen that President Tinubu has actually expressed deepest love for the state with the creation of the Nigerian Army 9 Division in Ilorin.

The duo, had earlier marched through the major streets of Ilorin to praise Tinubu for the gesture in the state

The Coordinator of Coalition of Kwara Youths, Mr. Ibrahim Saadu said, “The creation of the 9 Division is not just a military installation, it is an opportunity for economic development, an opportunity for job creation, improved security that will attract investors to our state and an opportunity for a better future, we must not waste this moment. We must support our security agencies.

“I am confident that with the establishment of the 9 Division, the days of insecurity in Kwara and neighbouring States are numbered, which is why we must appreciate and support President Tinubu and thank him, the Chief of Army Staff and the Chief of Defence Staff, for the creation of the 9 Division”.

Also, the Publicity Secretary of Arewa Youth Assembly, Mr. Aliyu Muhammad said, “The creation of 9 Division of Nigerian Army in Ilorin is not just a military decision, it is a strategic masterstroke.

“The establishment of this division will significantly enhance the security of lives and properties, it will improve command and control, strengthen border security, protect critical national infrastructure, and ensure faster military response to emerging threats.”

World.title: Air Chief Decries Misinformation, Hostile Narratives to Military Operations
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja





The Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has decried the menace of misinformation, disinformation and hostile narratives surrounding military operations, insisting that these digital vices undermined public confidence.

Aneke made the condemnation yesterday while declaring open the 2026 Directorate of Public Relations and Information (DOPRI) Annual Media Workshop and Meeting with Information Officers at the Headquarters of the Nigerian Air Force, Abuja.

The CAS, who was represented by the Chief of Policy and Plans (COPP), Nigerian Air Force, Air Vice Marshal Abubakar Yaro Abdullahi, said, “Today’s information environment is increasingly complex, dynamic and highly contested. News travels at unprecedented speed, while misinformation, disinformation and hostile narratives continue to challenge military operations and public confidence.

“In such an environment, effective public communication is no longer merely supportive; it is an operational necessity that contributes directly to mission success.

“As Information Officers, you represent the voice and image of the Nigerian Air Force. Your responsibilities extend beyond issuing press releases and organising media engagements.

“You are strategic communicators entrusted with shaping public understanding of our operations, projecting the professionalism of our personnel, preserving institutional credibility and strengthening public trust in the Service.

“Every communication, every engagement and every response to a crisis must therefore reflect accuracy, professionalism, integrity and timeliness.”

The Special Guest of Honour said the Service must remain proactive in communicating its activities with credibility, transparency and strategic intent while confronting evolving security challenges.

“We must continually improve our ability to engage stakeholders, counter misinformation, manage crises effectively and reinforce public confidence in the Service. Together, we can build a public relations and information system that reflects the professionalism, discipline and operational excellence for which the Nigerian Air Force is renowned,” he said.

World.title: Osun Security: Adeleke, New Police CP Seek Peace Building, State Reconciliation
World.content:
•Governor makes five requests

•I’ll drive a new beginning, police chief vows

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo





Osun state Governor, Ademola Adeleke and the police command, yesterday, held a new partnership meeting, with the governor making five requests for the police command to fulfil as pathway to restoring peace and normalcy to the state.

The newly posted police commissioner, Ibrahim Zungura, in company with top officials of the command, paid the governor a courtesy visit on his assumption of office, promising to restore faith in police among Osun people and serve Osun people for impartial law and order.

“I promise to work with the state government for peace and stability of the state. I will be fair to all and I will prove my commitment in the next few weeks. Osun is a peaceful state and we will work to address all outstanding issues,” the Zungura declared.

The state governor, in his response, recalled that the state had passed through turbulent times, noting that, “post-election peace is yet to be fully restored. A police operation today claimed two lives at Ikire. Your DPO for Ikire was fingered.

“Based on all details of the attacks, I request immediate commencement of disciplinary action against the DPO. He has become a threat to the people he was posted to protect.

“Our government is pushing to establish post- election peace and reconciliation initiatives. I have extended an olive branch to all stakeholders. You are posted to Osun at a very auspicious time. The police – civilian relationship is at the lowest ebb. The trust level is very disturbing.

“I therefore have specific requests as part of our efforts to consolidate peace and state reconciliation:

“Let us rebuild public trust in the police. You must make deliberate efforts to remove many areas of current police conduct that paints it as partisan and anti-people.

“Let’s strengthen the closer working relationship between the state government and the state police command. The government under my watch seeks no favour other than fair policing. Your partnership with our government for rule of law is solicited.

“Reorganise internal workings and operations of the state police command. I know you will be worried that Osun people see certain police units as the home base of APC thugs. There is a need to dissolve many police operational units because they have been compromised.

“Let us strengthen state security by full police participation at the State Security Council meetings. The last time your predecessor attended a state security council meeting was in 2024.

“I also call for the release of several Accord members arrested and indeterminate as political detainees. Further arrests of our members should also stop. Our government is ready to support police operations without any string attached. What we seek is fair policing,” the governor noted.

World.title: Kemi Omotosho: MultiChoice’s Business Transcends Entertainment
World.content:
MultiChoice Nigeria’s business has evolved beyond entertainment, with the company positioning itself as a broader participant in Nigeria’s creative economy, local talent, content production, technology and infrastructure, according to its Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho. Omotosho said that after more than three decades in Nigeria, MultiChoice had evolved from primarily bringing entertainment into Nigerian homes to becoming part of a wider ecosystem involving producers, actors, production crews, dealers, installers and small businesses.

“When people turn on DStv or GOtv, they see the finished product. What they don’t always see is the entire Nigerian ecosystem behind that screen

“We are not just distributing content; we are investing in the people, businesses and infrastructure that help Nigeria’s creative economy grow,” she said.

Her comments come as MultiChoice operates under a new ownership structure following its integration into CANAL+, the global media and entertainment group headquartered in France and operating across 70 countries, in September 2025. Omotosho said the new structure gives MultiChoice Nigeria access to greater scale, technology, content and international expertise while retaining its local focus.

“I would describe MultiChoice Nigeria as a deeply Nigerian business with the strength of a global group behind it,” she said.

According to her, the company’s products, content and commercial strategies remain shaped by Nigerian realities, while its local operation retains significant flexibility over products, pricing, distribution, content and customer experience.

“Nigeria is not a market where you can simply take something that works elsewhere and assume it will work here,” she said.

That local orientation is reflected in platforms such as Big Brother Naija and the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards, which showcase Nigerian and African stories, talent and culture to audiences across the continent.

The MultiChoice Talent Factory is also developing young filmmakers and production professionals, providing skills to help them build careers and businesses.

Omotosho said local investment was “fundamental” to MultiChoice’s future in Nigeria, adding that the company wanted to produce content Nigerians would be proud to watch while ensuring that Nigerian stories could travel across Africa and the world.

“Nigeria has the talent to be a global creative powerhouse, and we want MultiChoice to play an important role in making that happen,” she said.

She also linked the company’s fight against piracy to protecting the wider creative economy, arguing that piracy affects not only MultiChoice but producers, actors and the many workers whose livelihoods depend on content retaining commercial value.

According to her, MultiChoice is working with the Nigerian Copyright Commission and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy to curb piracy and educate the public about its wider consequences.

Omotosho said MultiChoice’s long presence in Nigeria remained an advantage as competition intensified across the entertainment industry, citing its established brands, strong local content, extensive distribution network and relationships with producers, creatives and partners.

But she acknowledged that longevity alone was insufficient.

“We still have to earn our customers every day by delivering great content, value, affordability and a strong customer experience,” she said.

For Omotosho, MultiChoice’s next phase is about combining the scale of its global ownership with the local knowledge and creative investment that have defined its Nigerian presence.

The ambition, she said, is to remain deeply connected to Nigeria while using the reach of its global group to take Nigerian talent, stories and creative products to wider audiences.

World.title: 2027: APC Disowns Hunye, Insists Yayi Remains Ogun Governorship Candidate
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja





The leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has disowned a self-declared governorship candidate, Mr. Abayomi Hunye, insisting that Senator Adeola Olamilekan Yayi remained the party’s standard bearer for the 2027 governorship election in Ogun State.

National Secretary of the party, Senator Ajibola Basiru, described his self-declaration as false, unauthorised and mischievous, adding that Hunye was no longer a member of the APC because he had been suspended.

“The All Progressives Congress (APC), hereby informs the general public stakeholders, Ogun State Chapter and the good people of Ogun State that Mr. Abayomi Hunye is an impostor who is currently on suspension as a member of APC.

“His recent self-declaration as the governorship candidate of our great party for the 2027 election is completely false, unauthorised, and a mischievous act aimed at misleading the public.

“For the avoidance o f doubt, Mr. Abayomi Hunye is not a member of the APC in good standing. He was suspended from the Party o n April 7, 2026, following a petition from his Ward, Tube Ward, in Ipokia Local Government Area.

“The suspension was not arbitrary. It was a grassroots decision driven by the Ward Executives in Tube Ward, ratified b y the Ipokia Local Government Area, and formally approved b y the Ogun State Working Committee.”

The party’s scribe explained that Hunye’s suspension was ratified by the Ogun State Working Committee and communicated to the National headquarters.

The reasons adduced for his suspension included engaging in activities injurious to the image of the party; and deliberate actions aimed at causing disaffection and division among loyal members.

Consequently, Basru said that Hunye lacked the legal and moral standing to represent the APC in any capacity.

World.title: From waffles to pizza: Sundowns players diet revealed! [video]
World.content:
Reabetjoe Mokoko, a vibrant team dietician for Mamelodi Sundowns FC, opened up about the players diet during a recent episode of the King David Studio Podcast.

Her passion for food and nutrition goes beyond cooking; she is pedantic about “how it is cooked, how it is eaten, and how much of it is eaten.”

She holds three degrees from Wits University, and her business partner oversees her side business while she works her magic in the Sundowns kitchen.



WHAT DO MAMELODI SUNDOWNS PLAYERS EAT?

Speaking on preparation methods, Reabetjoe explained the importance of a versatile menu that caters to the players different tastes.

She broke down the menu into categories, outlining what players generally eat.

Match Day Minus One: On the day before the big match, players start carb-loading with breakfast that includes starches like breakfast potatoes, hash browns, and waffles.



For lunch, players continue to enjoy a wide range of carbs, such as spaghetti, rice, burger rolls, pizza, and fruits.

Pre-Match: This phase includes a fueling station stocked with carbs like dried nuts, fruits, and sweets to boost the players energy before the game. Through a partnership with Biogen, players also refuel with high-quality supplements during halftime.

Recovery Hour: Immediately after the game, Rea personally hands out the Recovery Smoothies that help with healing and recovery.



The Golden Hour: During this final phase, players indulge in what Reabetjoe refers to as “real food.”

THIS IS HOW REABETJOE BAGGED A JOB AT SUNDOWNS

Reabetjoe’s path to joining Sundowns was carved by divine intervention, as she had aspired to venture into the world of football.

That dream came true when she met coach Rhulani Mokwena on The Braai Show (SABC 1), where she worked as a food stylist.



During their chat, Rhulani shared his concerns about the nutrition at Sundowns and said he needed someone like her to raise it to the best level.

RADICAL CHANGES YIELD POSITIVE RESULTS

Reabetjoe made radical changes in the Sundowns kitchen, starting with the breakfast menu. She replaced processed staples such as Russians with healthier alternatives such as mince, chicken strips, beef patties, and chicken livers.

This new diet struck a chord with the players, leading to weight loss and improved energy and performance.

World.title: From field to fatherhood: Vincent Tshituka becomes a dad! [photos]
World.content:
Katlego and Vincent Tshituka have welcomed their new baby. Images via IG

Springbok and Sharks player Vincent Tshituka is a proud new dad after welcoming a baby with his wife, Katlego.

The 27-year-old – who made his national team debut last year – and his partner recently celebrated their first wedding anniversary.

VINCENT TSHITUKA IS A FIRST-TIME DAD!

On his Instagram account, Vincent Tshituka made an exciting announcement – his wife, Katlego, had recently given birth to their first child.



Posting pics of both mom and dad embracing their baby, Vincent shared: “It’s so much bigger! Thank you God for a new purpose to live”.

The post was inundated with well-wishes, including those from fellow Springboks Ox Nche, Jese Kriel, and Jordn Hendrikse, amongst others.

The Tshitukas have yet to announce the baby’s gender or name.



Last month, the couple celebrated their first wedding anniversary. In May, they announced that they were expecting a baby.

COUNTDOWN FOR SPRINGBOK RG SNYMAN

Meanwhile, fellow Springbok RG Snyman and his wife, Saskia, are also awaiting the birth of their baby.



The player, nicknamed “The Viking”, and his partner have shared glimpses of her pregnancy on their social media accounts.

Like Vincent Sthituka, RG – who has returned to Ireland amid an ACL injury – is also set to become a first-time father.

World.title: Born and bred in SA : Meet Tharina Botes, Miss Universe Thailand
World.content:
South African-born model Tharina Botes has won Miss Universe Thailand. Images via IG

South African-born model and former Miss SA finalist, Tharina Botes, has been crowned Miss Universe Thailand.

The beauty queen and businesswoman was born in Randburg to a South African father and Thai mother.

Tharina moved abroad in 2019 at the age of 22.

THARINA BOTES CROWNED MISS UNIVERSE THAILAND

Over the weekend, Tharina Botes added another pageant title to her name – Miss Universe Thailand



Tharina, representing Bangkok, was awarded a diamond crown, a cash prize, sponsorship deals and the opportunity to represent Thailand at the Miss Universe pageant on 24 November in Puerto Rico.

“Dreams really come true”, the 29-year-old model and businesswoman shared in an Instagram post.

In another, Tharina added that convinced that hearing a Tyla song during the competition was a “sign”.



WHO IS THE SOUTH AFRICAN-BORN STUNNER?

Tharina Bortes was born and raised in Roodepoort to a South African father and Thai mother.

She attended Monument High School in Krugersdorp and became involved in modelling and pageantry as a teenager. She studied a BCom at Damelin College and later pursued economics through UNISA.

In her early days, she won Miss Teen Gauteng and Miss Rand Show, and represented South Africa at Miss International in Tokyo



In 2018, she entered the Miss South Africa pageant at the age of 21. The pageant, which included finalists like Bryoni Govender and Margo Fargo, was won by Tamaryn Green.

After the pageant, Tharina Botes moved to Thailand, where she continued pageantry.

Tharin won Miss Grand Phuket and Miss Thailand World in 2019 and 2023, respectively.



Before winning the title of Miss Unirsee Thailand, she was named first runner-up in 2021.

World.title: Orlando Pirates star Maswanganyi moves overseas
World.content:
Patrick Maswanganyi celebrates scoring for Orlando Pirates in the MTN8. Image: Official PSL

Orlando Pirates confirmed that an agreement had been reached with the Bahraini club. The club revealed Maswanganyi expressed his desire to continue his career abroad.

His departure brings an end to a spell in which he established himself as a popular figure among the Orlando Pirates supporters.

PATRICK MASWANGANYI GETS ORLANDO PIRATES FAREWELL

Maswanganyi remained an important part of the technical team’s plans for the new season. However, discussions between the player, his representatives and the club ultimately led to Orlando Pirates agreeing to allow him to pursue the opportunity overseas.



The club confirmed that the 28-year-old Maswanganyi’s decision was respected despite his importance to the squad.

“In recognition of his service to the Club and his ambitions for the next chapter of his career, Orlando Pirates agreed not to stand in his way,” the club said.

A transfer was subsequently concluded with Alkhaldiya Sports Club, allowing Maswanganyi to begin a new chapter in Bahrain.



“Tito” leaves Orlando Pirates as a league champion and a firm favourite among the Ghost. His performances in the famous black and white jersey earned him a special place among the supporters.

The club also highlighted his commitment to representing Orlando Pirates with pride throughout his time in Soweto.

Also read: Latest report: SAFA make decision on Pitso Mosimane



THE BUCCANEERS THANK TITO

Maswanganyi departs having made a lasting impression both on and off the field. His personality and performances made him a popular member of the Buccaneers squad.

“From his first appearance in the famous black and white jersey, he gave the Ghost countless moments to celebrate and represented this club with pride,” Orlando Pirates said.

His exit will now leave the technical team with another important squad decision as the club continues its campaign across domestic competitions.



Orlando Pirates thanked the playmaker for his dedicated service and wished him success in the next chapter of his career.

The club added: “He departs as a league champion, a firm favourite among the supporters and a player who understood the responsibility of representing Orlando Pirates Football Club.”

Maswanganyi will now look to make his mark in the Bahrain Premier League after closing the door on his Orlando Pirates chapter.

World.title: SA passport holders can travel to these 101 countries without a visa
World.content:
SA passport holders can travel to 101 destinations without obtaining a visa in advance, according to the latest Henley Passport Index. Image: Allianz Travel Insurance

Holders of a South African passport can travel to 101 destinations without obtaining a visa in advance, according to the latest edition of the Henley Passport Index compiled by Henley & Partners.

The updated ranking places South Africa 96th out of 199 passports globally, with a visa-free score of 101.

The index evaluates passports based on the number of countries their holders can enter without needing to obtain a visa before departure.



It covers 199 passports and 227 travel destinations, making it one of the most widely cited indicators of global mobility.

Where does South Africa rank?

With a visa-free score of 101, South Africa’s passport ranks behind Qatar, which offers access to 112 destinations, and is one ahead of Belize in the global standings.

The ranking means South African travellers can visit 101 destinations with relative ease, although visas or advance authorisations are still required for many countries worldwide.

World’s Most Powerful Passports

According to the index, Asian and European countries continue to dominate global travel access.

Singapore holds the most powerful passport , with visa-free access to 192 destinations .

, with visa-free access to . Japan, South Korea and United Arab Emirates follow closely, each offering access to 188 destinations .

. Sweden ranks fifth, with a score of 187.

At the other end of the spectrum, Afghanistan remains the lowest-ranked passport, with access to only 22 destinations without a prior visa.

Measuring Global Mobility

The Henley Passport Index is widely used as a benchmark for global mobility.



The rankings reflect a range of factors including diplomatic relations, international agreements, and security considerations, all of which influence visa policies between countries.

Three Types of Visa Access

The 101 destinations available to South African passport holders fall into three main travel categories:

Visa-Free Access: Travellers can enter the destination simply by presenting their passport at immigration, with no advance application required.

Travellers can enter the destination simply by presenting their passport at immigration, with no advance application required. Visa on Arrival: Visitors can obtain a visa at the airport or border entry point, often after paying a fee.

Visitors can obtain a visa at the airport or border entry point, often after paying a fee. Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA): Travellers must complete a short online application before departure but do not need to visit an embassy or consulate.

While the 2026 ranking highlights moderate global mobility for South Africans, it also underscores the gap between South Africa’s travel access and that enjoyed by holders of the world’s most powerful passports.
