World.title: Nearly 1,900 basic school graduates still lack a school place as year begins
World.content:
A week before the start of the new school year, 1,893 basic school graduates in Estonia are without a school place; of them, 761 live in Tallinn, said Kadi Serbak, adviser at the Ministry of Education (HTM).

According to Serbak, HTM monitors the situation of finding school places daily. Since continued admissions to schools are still underway, HTM does not yet have a complete overview of young people who have not found a new study place after finishing basic school. Schools must enter admitted students into the Estonian Education Information System, from which HTM can see how many students are still without a school place.

HTM's project manager for compulsory education, Külli Solo, said that many schools do not do this during the admissions process, and there are young people who have received a school place but have not been entered into the information system.

The final number of basic school graduates who will not continue their studies will be known around 10 September. According to HTM data, in previous years about 800 basic school graduates have not continued their studies. The forecast is the same for this year.

Serbak said the ministry is trying to find solutions to the current situation in cooperation with local governments.

The ministry is analysing how to make basic school graduation and finding school places smoother and less stressful next year. "We have also informed the city of Tallinn that we would like to discuss options for increasing the number of preparatory study places ordered at Tallinn Applied College," Serbak said.

Continued admissions underway

Ülle Matsin, head of HTM's department of general and vocational education, told ERR last week that schools are conducting continued admissions every day, which means that eventually all students will find a study place.

"There is definitely a study place available to fulfil compulsory education, and if students currently still need counselling, they can confidently contact the schools where admissions are still ongoing," Matsin said.

"All learners will find opportunities to study. Through cooperation between the state and the city, study places in Tallinn should ultimately be available for all students," she confirmed.

Tallinn deputy mayor Andrei Kante said last week that the reason so many young people still lack clarity about their study options at the end of August is that basic school is being completed by young people without learning skills.

Matsin agreed that basic education holds several keys: a basic school graduate should receive guidance on where to continue studying and be aware that vocational fields offer many learning opportunities.

"We have actually pointed this out earlier in our messaging — that career counselling in basic school is important, and preparing the student at the end of the third school stage to move forward is crucial. In that respect, he is undoubtedly right," the ministry official said.

Tartu also has young people without school places

As of Friday, Tartu had around one hundred young people who have not found a school place, have not looked for one, or have left Estonia altogether, such as Ukrainian war refugees. This number is still constantly changing, said Riho Raave, head of Tartu's education department.

He said continued admissions are underway in some upper secondary schools and vocational institutions in Tartu, such as Tartu Applied College and Tartu Art School. "Applications are ongoing and the process is still underway, so I think by 1 September there will be even fewer who have not found a study place," Raave noted.

In connection with compulsory education, preparatory study will also begin for the first time this academic year. It is intended for young people up to age 18 who need support after basic school to move on to the next level of education.

According to Raave, the problem in Tartu is that all state‑funded preparatory study places at both Tartu Art School and the Applied College are already full.

Raave said schools had the option to admit students to preparatory study on their own. "Students applied, schools accepted them, but now there are no preparatory study places left for the most complex group of students — those who cannot find a school place," he explained. Raave believes more places need to be created.

Preparatory study should be an extreme measure

Solo said that ongoing continued admissions may still bring changes to preparatory study places, but negotiations with local governments are underway regarding the number of study places.

"Preparatory study is an extreme measure, intended specifically for those 800 young people who do not continue studying," Solo said.

In early August, it became clear that HTM wants to begin admissions to preparatory study next year starting from 1 September — that is, after basic and continued admissions. This should ensure that preparatory study is offered only to those young people who do not have a study place by 1 September or who need additional support.

World.title: Financial Intelligence Unit awaits restoration of powers by Riigikogu
World.content:
A bill aimed at clarifying the Financial Intelligence Unit's (FIU) access to banking data and restoring its ability to conduct on-site inspections has passed its first reading in the Riigikogu.

The final vote could come as early as October. Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, now the only formally registered presidential candidate, has endorsed the bill and, if it passes and she is elected president, it could end up on her desk for assent or veto.

The bill would address two major restrictions on the FIU: its ability to access bank account information through the enforcement register and its ability to carry out on-site inspections at banks and other institutions.

The legislation follows concerns raised by Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise about the legal basis for government agencies accessing bank account information through the enforcement register. The unit's access was suspended by Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200).

The restrictions also affected the Tax and Customs Board (MTA), which was unable to request certain data through the register for tax-fraud prevention and other duties until the government reversed course in May.

The government has since proposed amendments specifying when and how the FIU and MTA may request banking data through the enforcement register. The Finance Ministry has stressed that the amendments do not create new substantive powers to access banking secrecy, but clarify that existing powers may be exercised through the enforcement register, a secure and logged channel.

Under the proposed framework, requests would have to be justified and logged, while people would have the ability to challenge an administrative act authorising access.

The Estonian-founded LHV Pank, for example, has stopped providing bank account statements to the FIU, saying the unit has no legal right to request them. The Tallinn Administrative Court ruled in the bank's favor, although the FIU has appealed.

FIU chief Matis Mäeker said the restrictions are also affecting Estonia's ability to cooperate with its international partners, and that this is harming Estonia in return.

In her role as Chancellor of Justice, Ülle Madise raised concerns which led to a diminishing of the FIU's powers. However, a bill restoring them could end up being signed by her if it passes and if she gets elected president in early September. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

"If you are a good partner, you get answers more quickly; if you are a worse partner, you get answers more slowly. At the moment, we are in a situation where we cannot answer all questions as we do not have the right to request this data," Mäeker said.

Mäeker gave as an example one case in which fraudulently obtained money was transferred to another country one day, then by the following day had already been moved to accounts at 14 different credit institutions, making recovering the funds increasingly difficult.

The FIU's powers were further restricted by a Supreme Court ruling in January. The body can no longer physically visit, for example, a bank or a gambling company, in order to check compliance with its anti-money-laundering (AML) procedures.

On-site inspections are an "irreplaceable" tool for a supervisory authority, Mäeker added.

"One thing is what happens on paper, another is what happens in real life. To understand whether what is on paper actually corresponds to reality, you can only find out on site," he said.

The bill would address both issues. It would clarify the division and extent of the powers of the FIU and MTA to obtain information needed for their duties, particularly bank account and account data, while also restoring the FIU's ability to conduct on-site inspections.

The opposition parties have signaled support for the bill, though some MPs have questioned its lengthy notification deadlines. Aivar Kokk (Isamaa), a member of the Riigikogu Finance Committee, said he could not understand how it could ever be justified to keep a person unaware for so long that their bank account had been examined. Andrei Korobeinik (Center) warned that notification could potentially be postponed repeatedly.

Under the terms of the bill, a person or company would normally be notified five years after their bank account statement was obtained. In certain circumstances, notification could be postponed for up to another five years — meaning that in some cases, the person or company might not learn about the examination for as long as 10 years.

Maris Lauri (Reform), who is leading work on the bill in the Finance Committee, said she wants to hear further justification from interest groups regarding the time limits. She noted that the current deadlines may be optimal, but discussions are continuing. If consideration proceeds without major obstacles, the Riigikogu could adopt the bill as early as October.

FIU chief Matis Mäeker. Source: ERR

LHV has raised broader privacy and legal concerns about the proposed rules. Ants Soone, LHV's head of compliance, wrote that since 2021 the FIU has no longer been an investigative body and lacks the right to conduct surveillance measures. He argued that treating the examination of bank statements as a surveillance measure could raise questions about whether evidence obtained in this way would be admissible in court.

Soone also objected to the possibility of retaining information covered by bank confidentiality for five to 10 years "just in case," arguing that mass retention of personal data like this could conflict with EU fundamental-rights law.

Madise has also weighed in, saying she did not oppose the bill in principle. She agreed that the FIU and/or the MTA should be able to access bank account statements via the enforcement register when investigating specific suspicions, but said the Riigikogu should carefully consider whether the proposed notification periods are truly necessary or should be shortened.

If the bill passes, it would address concerns Madise raised as Chancellor of Justice. Madise is, at the time of writing, the only formally registered candidate in the presidential elections taking place in the Riigikogu, with a few hours to go until registration closes. If the 74 MPs who signed in favour of her candidacy — or a minimum of 68 MPs — translate that backing into a vote for Madise as president on September 2-3, she will become the next head of state.

If that happened, she would then have the power as president to sign or veto legislation on the same topic herself.

The money laundering bill's final reading may take place in October, as things stand.

World.title: Kaamos art grant to focus on artists over 60
World.content:
The Kaamos art scholarship, awarded for the first time last year, is this year intended for artists over 60. The amount of the scholarship is 25,000 euros.

While the focus in the first year was on women artists, Kaamos has now decided that the scholarship's target group will change each year in order to draw attention to different groups within the Estonian art field and their work, and to keep the scholarship diverse and evolving over time.

The Kaamos art scholarship was established by the Estonian Centre for Contemporary Art and Estonian-owned investment firm Kaamos Group. Candidates are invited to apply until 28 September; artists may apply themselves or be nominated by someone working in the art field or by an art institution.

The recipient will be chosen by a jury consisting of Kumu curator Eha Komissarov, head of Tartu Art House and chair of the Tartu Artists' Union Peeter Talvistu, artist and artist‑salary recipient Marge Monko, one representative of the CCA and two representatives of Kaamos Group. The composition of the jury rotates partially every two years.

Last year, the first Kaamos scholarship was awarded to Anna Mari Liivrand. "The Kaamos scholarship came unexpectedly and at a very right moment for me," said last year's laureate. "With the support of the scholarship, I have been able to fully dedicate myself to both larger and smaller exhibition projects, and I see that it has helped me create more substantial and exciting works."

World.title: Government to begin next year's budget talks on Tuesday
World.content:
The government will begin discussions on next year's budget and the state budget strategy at Stenbock House on Tuesday.

Deputy director of government communications Liis Velsker said that on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, members of the government will start discussions on next year's state budget and the state budget strategy for the next four years.

On Thursday, the Ministry of Finance will present the summer economic forecast to the cabinet.

The economic forecast is used by the government and parliament when making budget‑policy decisions, and by businesses when preparing strategic plans. The explanatory memorandum also gives the wider public an overview of recent economic developments and the outlook for the next four years.

"Over the coming weeks, the government will discuss the budget. At the end of September, the government will approve the revenue, expenditure and other measures of the state budget and the state budget strategy, as well as the Health Insurance Fund's budget position for the next four years, and all draft laws related to next year's state budget. The goal is also to approve the allocation of EU support for the 2028–2034 period — the state plan," Velsker said.

She added that at the end of September, the government must submit the draft state budget for 2027 to the Riigikogu and approve the state budget strategy for 2027–2030. Before that, the government will hear the opinion of the Fiscal Council.

World.title: ISS calls for dedicated law to standardize background checks
World.content:
An internal security advisory to the interior minister urges basic background checks for people in critical posts, a need heightened by recent security developments. Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS) calls for a separate law to resolve the legal issues.

Each year, the security agencies present the interior minister with their view on what the state should do to ensure internal security and public safety.

In this year's advisory, ISS notes that the need to conduct background checks for employees in critical positions has risen sharply due to Russia's aggressive behavior, highlighting the defense‑industry sector as one example. The legal basis for conducting such checks should be set out in a dedicated background‑check law, said ISS spokesperson Marta Tuul.

"A general regulation would help ensure security more effectively. Right now, background checks are carried out under several special laws — the Aviation Act, the Imprisonment Act, the Defence Forces Organization Act, the Police and Border Guard Act, and others. These all cover different fields, meaning their requirements and guidelines differ and are not uniform," Tuul explained.

She added that background checks are already conducted for applicants to higher‑risk positions, and ISS does not see a need to expand that circle.

"In recent years — due to the security situation and the war in Ukraine — the number of background checks has increased year by year, but expanding the scope is not necessary," Tuul said.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200). Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Interior minister Igor Taro, however, said that additional positions requiring background checks have emerged.

"We have developed sensitive positions involving state secrets, and we have looked much more closely at whom we hire for critical infrastructure related to essential services — there are certain positions there that also require checks," Taro said.

Amendments to the Emergency Act that took effect in 2024 expanded the list of essential service providers. Estonia now has 22 essential services provided by more than 400 companies. The most recent additions include family‑doctor services, the supply of medicines and food, aeronautical navigation, airports, ports and public railway services. Under the Emergency Act, candidates for critical positions in such services must undergo background checks.

An employer or state institution cannot conduct a background check arbitrarily — there must be a direct legal basis, and the person must be informed that a background check will be carried out.

World.title: Riga and Vilnius outpace Tallinn in flights due to market size
World.content:
Although Tallinn has fewer direct destinations, Tallinn Airport is still the largest airport in the Baltics in terms of revenue, surpassing both Latvia and Lithuania, says airport chief Riivo Tuvike. Last year Tallinn Airport's revenue was 74 million euros.

This success comes from the fact that Tallinn Airport does not rely solely on aviation fees, which make up only about 30% of its income. The company actively earns revenue from terminal retail, parking, aircraft maintenance hangars and commercial real estate in Airport City.

Tallinn Airport has also experienced a historic surge in passenger numbers this summer, driven by expanding flight options and more affordable ticket prices.

The airport shattered its all-time passenger records during June and July. Tuvike noted that in July, the airport welcomed 384,000 passengers, representing a 19 percent increase compared to the previous year. The appetite for travel has not disappeared since the pandemic, and higher local wealth combined with lower prices has fueled this growth.

Looking at history, in 1991 Tallinn Airport had 758,000 passengers, but the following year, 1992, only about 205,000, so there was a large drop. "Looking at the current year, we believe we will reach 3.7–3.8 million passengers, which is quite a noticeable increase," Tuvike said.

The long-term goal is serving five million travelers annually by 2030.

Passenger volume dictates the decisions

When asked why the airport does not aggressively lower its fees to attract even more airlines, Tuvike points out that market demand and passenger volume — not just cheap airport fees — ultimately dictate an airline's route decisions.

"We could lower the fees even to zero, but if there are no passengers, the airlines will not open those routes," Tuvike said.

"Perhaps our concern in Tallinn is that the region we are able to serve is only about one million passengers. In the end, the number of potential passengers dictates how many possible direct routes there can be," he noted.

Riivo Tuvike Autor/allikas: Iris Tähema/ERR

Despite the current positive passenger trends, the regional aviation market faces challenges, particularly concerning the financial health of Latvian carrier airBaltic. AirBaltic remains Estonia's most important airline and operates as a home carrier, but Tuvike believes the Estonian government should not buy a stake in the struggling airline.

The entire Baltic region is a very small area in a global scale, Tuvike said. He added that operating a profitable airline in such a limited market is extremely difficult and suggested there are more reasonable areas for state investment.

The airport chief reassured travelers that even if airBaltic were to exit the market, Estonia's flight connections would not collapse. He explained that Tallinn has actively diversified its airline portfolio, such as by facilitating the expansion of low-cost carrier Wizz Air, to ensure that routes can be replaced if necessary.

The rapid growth in passenger traffic has placed significant strain on the existing airport infrastructure. The current terminal was designed to handle up to three million passengers, meaning the current volume is already causing operational friction, including baggage wait times that can reach an hour.

Major expansion of the Tallinn airport ongoing

To address these bottlenecks, the airport is planning a major physical expansion. Tuvike said that while new check-in kiosks have already been installed, the main construction work is scheduled to begin early next year. The project aims to expand the passenger terminal by 50 percent by the first half of 2029, with a specific focus on enlarging the overcrowded baggage claim and border control areas.

Regarding flight destinations, Tuvike emphasized that major hubs remain the most critical connections for Estonian travelers because they open access to the rest of the world. Currently, Warsaw has emerged as the number one destination, with Frankfurt, Riga, and Helsinki also making up the majority of flights.

Tuvike mentioned that while direct flights largely dictate where Estonians go on vacation, his future target destinations for direct flights from Tallinn include London Heathrow and Madrid.

"London Heathrow is definitely a place where we really want to go, because there are so many flight opportunities and it contributes strongly to Estonia's connection," Tuvike said.

Tuvike also addressed the future of Estonia's regional airports, noting that while airports on the country's islands are fully justified due to the lack of fast land transport, the future of mainland facilities like Pärnu Airport is less certain. He pointed out that once the Rail Baltica railway is completed, Pärnu will be just a 45-minute journey from Tallinn, making the local airport's role highly questionable.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Infantino
World.content:
Paris – Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian football federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF — which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean — have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

World.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing’ as US threatens ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

“IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!” the president posted Monday in his trademark all-caps style on his social media platform Truth Social.

His remarks came hours after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a column for the Financial Times, declared that an “economic D-Day” had begun against Tehran and warned that any country that continued to enable the Islamic republic would become a “global pariah”.

Bessent also claimed on X that the US had “dismantled Iran’s military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme”.

Iran responded with defiance, saying the latest US measures were an admission of military defeat, and it warned countries against aiding Washington.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the US turn to financial warfare proved Bessent’s claims false.

“Your narrative doesn’t add up,” Gharibabadi said, asking why, if Washington had achieved its goals, “there is a need for ‘the largest financial invasion in history’ and the mobilisation of ‘all institutions and powers’ of the United States!

“Is this a victory or an admission of America’s defeat?”

The US and Israel linked the launch of their war in February to Iran’s nuclear programme, but the focus since the early days of fighting has been on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.

Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and heaping domestic pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.

– Oil exports plunge –

Bessent was due to set out details of the US plan on Monday, but it is unclear how much more economic pressure Washington can put on Tehran.

The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.

Meanwhile, the country has been under crushing international sanctions for decades, with a brief period of easing under a 2015 nuclear deal that Trump later ripped up as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign.

The Islamic republic has weathered those efforts and, before the war, continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

Bessent and Trump have both warned countries against helping Iran, signalling a shift in their focus, with the Treasury secretary’s FT column dwelling on nations who “appease” and “enable” Iran.

Tehran responded on Monday by warning countries not to cooperate with the US efforts. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said taking part would “definitely have its own consequences”.

For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.

Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, put it simply: “It’s really very difficult. I don’t think people can really take this much longer.”

On Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admitted that Iran faced “many problems in society”.

“We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride,” Pezeshkian said.

– Delegation from Pakistan –

Last week, the Iranian president, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should “bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity”.

That followed supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointing hardliners to key security positions.

Hassanbeigi said she wanted peace. “Naturally, negotiations mean that both sides have to compromise. My personal opinion is that Iran should compromise now,” she told AFP.

Throughout the war, diplomatic efforts, pushed on by mediators, have sought a negotiated end to the conflict.

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief was expected in Iran. Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi was also due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

World.title: Liverpool must improve on ‘unacceptable’ season, says Van Dijk
World.content:
Liverpool – Virgil van Dijk said Liverpool “need to show a reaction” from a bitterly disappointing season that cost Arne Slot his job as manager, but called for patience with new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds needed a 99th-minute equaliser from the penalty spot by Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Slot guided Liverpool to glory and a 20th league title in his debut campaign in 2024/25, but paid the price for finishing fifth last season when he was dismissed in May.

Many of the same flaws were in evidence in Iraola’s first outing at St James’ Park as Newcastle sliced open the Liverpool defence on the counter-attack.

But they twice came from behind to avoid a losing start to the new season.

“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession, work, whatever you do, if you come in new and you have new plans and new ideas, then it takes a bit of time with new players,” said Van Dijk.

“It’s down to us to do it as soon as we can, as soon as possible, because we want to improve, we want to win, we want to be better. That’s what we are going to try to do.

“We need to show a reaction from last year, that we are much better than last year, because this was very unacceptable.”

Iraola has not been aided by a lack of new arrivals in the transfer market.

Despite the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah and a long-term injury to Hugo Ekitike, Liverpool have only added Spanish winger Victor Munoz in attacking areas as well as defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Paris Saint-Germain’s two-time Champions League winner Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Anfield, while two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh have reportedly been turned down.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless and I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions,” Van Dijk added.

“That’s the only thing I can say, so let’s see what we are going to do.”

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.title: Prevent misuse of data by private entities, SC tells government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.

Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.

Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers.

No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".

Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.





SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."

World.title: Mizoram's 'misogynistic' marriage, divorce law faces challenge in SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Entrepreneur and Congress functionary Meriam L Hrangchal Monday challenged the constitutional validity of Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act, 2014, which was enacted by Congress govt headed by Lal Thanhawla, terming it "misogynistic and pro-Mizo men".

Hrangchal, daughter of former deputy CM Lalhmingthanga, told a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant that the law, which codified customary law, applied to any person belonging to a Mizo tribe and extended to marriages where the male member belonged to a Mizo tribe.

The 2014 Act denies Mizo women, who marry outside the Mizo community, access to a comprehensive community-specific statutory framework governing marriage, property and inheritance, thereby infringing their right to equality, dignity and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21, she said.

The law marginalises the independent identity of Mizo women and refuses them the benefits under the 2014 Act which extends to marriage between a Mizo man and a non-Mizo woman but does not cover marriage between a Mizo woman and a non-Mizo man, she said, citing her own marital relationship.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The effect of such provisions is that Mizo women who marry non-Mizo men, and the children born out of such marriages, are excluded from the statutory regime, notwithstanding their subsisting connection to the Mizo community," she said.





The bench said the issue raised in her petition was important but asked why she was bypassing the high court. Her counsel said the community being small, she feared for her safety if her petition was heard by the Aizawl bench of Gauhati HC.

The CJI-led bench understood her apprehension and requested the CJ of Gauhati HC to hear her petition in Guwahati without sending it to the Aizawl bench.

World.title: 22 million hectares of degraded land restored during 2011 and 2020
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has restored nearly 22 million hectares of degraded and deforested land during the 2011-20 period as against its target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030, said Union minister

at a UN conference Monday.

While addressing the 17th session (COP17) of the UNCCD conference in Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, he also pitched for "diversified, adequate, predictable and sustained international finance" for land restoration and drought resilience, saying it is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihood and long-term resilience.

Underlining how the country's restoration efforts had generated approximately 1.2 billion person-days of employment during the 2011-20 period, he said these figures demonstrated restoration could deliver both environmental and socio-economic outcomes by reviving degraded landscapes while creating employment and supporting rural livelihoods.

According to Indiaâs second progress report on its land restoration efforts, covering the period 2011â2020, Telangana restored the maximum (4.2 million hectares) degraded area followed by Madhya Pradesh (3.8 million ha), Odisha (2.6 million ha), Gujarat (1.7 million ha) and Andhra Pradesh (1.6 million ha) through afforestation, water resource management, sustainable farming practices, agroforestry, mangrove restoration and natural regeneration of formerly forested land.





Indiaâs Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas shows that 97.8 million ha of land, or nearly 29.8% of the countryâs geographical area, are affected by land degradation and desertification. Around 82% of Indiaâs degraded land falls in nine states/UT - Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

World.title: Amit Shah focuses on new doctrine to fight terror & radicalisation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union home minister

Monday emphasised enhanced training for implementing the country's first-ever counter-terrorism and counter-radicalisation doctrine, Prahaar, and expediting trial in cases with cross-border linkages by bringing back fugitives and using trial in absentia to bring foreign-based masterminds to justice.

In his inaugural address at the two-day National Security Strategies Conference, being attended by over 850 officials from the security forces, agencies and police forces, Shah directed that an artificial intelligence-based analysis of information available on multi-agency centre (MAC) platforms be done to create standard operating procedures to counter various security challenges.

The Union minister instructed all the agencies to take strict measures against infiltration and asked police forces to adopt a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act cases.

The first day of the conference focused on discussing critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges; fusion, analysis and operationalisation of intelligence through MAC; vision document on narcotics control; detection and deportation of illegal migrants; a policy framework to combat cyber-crime; and proxy warfare by Pakistan.

On Tuesday, the conference will deliberate on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security, and the need for a bio-security framework.





Prior to inaugurating the conference, the home minister paid tribute at the martyrs' column here, honouring the supreme sacrifice of Intelligence Bureau personnel to safeguard national security and integrity.

The conference, being held in hybrid format, was attended by junior home ministers, deputy NSAs, heads of central paramilitary forces, DGPs of states and UTs, young cops working at the cutting-edge level and experts from specialised fields.

World.title: SC to consider Tarun Tejpal's plea for exemption from surrender
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Monday said it would pass order on former Tehelka editor

's plea seeking exemption from surrender after Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case, with Goa govt opposing his plea and contending that his appeal was not admissible since the convict had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

The matter was heard by a single judge, Justice Alok Aradhe. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state govt, contended that existence of the appeal was dependent on Tejpal either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, requesting the court to allow an exemption from surrender.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, representing Tejpal, said there was no need to surrender yet since the high court itself had granted him time to surrender.

"This rule doesn't apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule. Suppose the court says no stay, I will have to go to jail," Sibal said, requesting the court to list the appeal for Aug 31.

After hearing both sides, Justice Aradhe said he would pass an appropriate order in the matter.

The Goa bench of Bombay high court convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of the IPC and sentenced him to 10 years rigorous imprisonment each under sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently. It also imposed additional concurrent sentences for offences relating to outraging a woman's modesty, sexual harassment, disrobing, wrongful restraint and wrongful confinement. The fines imposed on Tejpal total Rs 10.1 lakh, which the court directed to be paid to the victim.

World.title: 3 Bambiha members deported from Malaysia
World.content:
Three Bambiha gang operatives deported from Malaysia in major crackdown, says Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: In a major operation against the Bambiha criminal network, Indian agencies have executed a coordinated crackdown on its key overseas operatives, deporting three of its members from Malaysia who were ordering hits and carrying out extortions in India on behalf of the group's kingpin Lucky Patial.Announced by Union home minister Amit Shah on X Monday, the high-profile action targeted Jaspreet Singh (alias Jas Behbal) of Faridkot, alongside Ajay Singh (alias Ajay Malaysia) and Pawandeep Singh, both from Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district.
